resources.description: First Place–Phoenix is a supportive apartment community at 3001 N. Third St. in midtown Phoenix for adults with autism and other neurodiversities. It offers one- and two-bedroom suites with a suite of supports and amenities, on-site employment preparation and community-life programs, plus a separate two-year residential Transition Academy run with the Southwest Autism Research & Resource Center (SARRC). It is not a group home or assisted-living facility. Call 602-464-6600 or email info@firstplaceaz.org to ask about availability, rents, tours and eligibility.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
* Supportive independent-living apartments in midtown Phoenix (one- and two-bedroom suites) with sensory-friendly design, smart-home technology and shared community spaces; daily community-life activities; on-site employment support (interview preparation, job search, public-transit navigation); health and wellness programming.
* The website currently advertises "Now Leasing: 2026 Supportive Living Apartments."
* A separate two-year residential Transition Academy, operated with SARRC, provides independent-living and career-readiness training (Learn4Independence curriculum, individualized services, clinical assessment).
* The property states it is not a group home or a licensed congregate-care or assisted-living facility and is not designed for people who need a medical home.

**Eligibility Requirements**
* Apartments: built for adults with autism and/or other neurodiversities; rental and income requirements apply — ask First Place for current tenant-selection criteria and the application process.
* Transition Academy (training program): age 18+ with high school or learning-resource program completion; autism diagnosis; basic self-care and medication management with oversight; ability to communicate needs and participate in small-group learning; no current or chronic addiction or serious mental illness; no severe aggression, self-injury or property destruction in the past 12 months; able to function safely without direct supervision during unstructured time; motivated to participate. SARRC completes the clinical determination.
* A subset of income-targeted units has been reported (about 16); ask how those units are allocated and what income limits apply.

**Population Served**
* Adults with autism and/or other neurodiversities (residents have ranged from their early 20s to mid-40s); Transition Academy participants are adults with autism (18+). Supports are designed for people who can live with limited supervision.

**How to Best Connect**
* Call 602-464-6600 or email info@firstplaceaz.org; tours and inquiries can be scheduled through the website ("Schedule Tour" / Tour & Inquire).
* Address: 3001 N. Third St., Phoenix, AZ 85012 — midtown Phoenix, close to public transit.
* For the Transition Academy, the website outlines steps: schedule an overview meeting, take a tour, submit the registration form and fee, meet financial and rental requirements, complete the SARRC clinical determination and interview, then enroll.
* Ask directly about current apartment availability, waitlist, rents and leasing timeline, since availability changes.

**Important Information to Know**
* Costs: Transition Academy tuition is tuition-based (scholarship information is available); reported figures have ranged roughly $42,000–$89,000 per year for 2026 but were not confirmed — ask for current tuition and whether insurance, AHCCCS/DDD funding or scholarships can offset it. Apartment rents are separate; see "Floorplans & Pricing" or ask.
* Unit-count reports vary (55 units at opening; other accounts say the mid-60s) — confirm the current unit mix and what is available.
* Access limits: not a licensed care setting; people needing a medical home or intensive supervision are not a fit, and behavioral criteria apply for the Transition Academy.
* The "Now Leasing" status is from the website and can change — confirm before promising anything; no place is guaranteed.

resources.description: UPLIFT is a small permanent supportive housing program run by Florence Crittenton Services of Arizona in midtown Phoenix. It houses up to about six young women ages 18–25 who lack stable family support or left foster care early, with coaching in daily living, finances and job readiness plus counseling. Capacity is very limited and referrals appear to run through the agency or partner case managers rather than walk-in; contact the agency to confirm the current process and openings.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
* Permanent supportive housing for up to about six young women (ages 18–25) in midtown Phoenix, with ongoing coaching in day-to-day living skills, financial management and job readiness, plus counseling and support while residents build skills for independent living.
* Florence Crittenton Services of Arizona also provides other youth and family services (including behavioral-health and outpatient programs for youth) and, per nonprofit filings, owns a duplex rented to community tenants; the housing program described here is UPLIFT.

**Eligibility Requirements**
* Young women ages 18–25; many residents have no stable family support or left the state foster-care system early and need help with independent-living skills. Program descriptions also note young women parenting on their own.
* Specific admission criteria, referral requirements and any income rules are not published — confirm with the agency; a case-manager or agency referral appears likely rather than walk-in.

**Population Served**
* Young women ages 18–25 in the Phoenix area, including former foster youth, young women without stable family support and young mothers, per program descriptions.

**How to Best Connect**
* Contact Florence Crittenton Services of Arizona: website www.flocrit.org (contact page); email referrals@flocrit.org — published for the agency's residential programs — and ask specifically about UPLIFT housing referrals.
* Organization address: 1112 E. Buckeye Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85034; UPLIFT is described as located in midtown Phoenix.
* Ask whether a case manager, agency or coordinated-entry referral is required and what documents are needed. A current phone number for the program was not confirmed; the website and referral email are the safest first contacts.

**Important Information to Know**
* Capacity is very small (about six young women), and current openings or waits are not published — ask about both.
* Costs: no fees or rent details are published; ask what residents pay and whether any subsidy applies.
* Published details on UPLIFT are limited and may be dated; confirm the program is currently operating and taking referrals before promising a bed.
* The organization is described in community profiles as affiliated with Chicanos Por La Causa; confirm if relevant.
* No eligibility or placement is guaranteed.

resources.description: Foster360 provides safe housing and wraparound support for young adults who have aged out of foster care, with housing in Mesa and Tempe and services across the East Valley. Support includes case management, life-skills workshops, education and employment help, therapy, transportation and basic needs. Contact info@foster360az.org or 480-834-2115; the website's "Need Help?" section says it supports ages 18–23 who have transitioned from foster care.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
* Safe, stable housing for young adults transitioning out of foster care at two East Valley facilities — a Mesa campus ("Stage One") and a Tempe campus ("Stage Two & Three") — in a trauma-informed, community-centered environment.
* Wraparound services: case management, life-skills workshops (cooking, financial literacy, health advocacy, healthy relationships), education and employment support (GED preparation, resume building, interviews, job placement), individual and group counseling, therapeutic services through partners (including art, music, physical, speech and occupational therapy, and support for traumatic brain injury), transportation help, and basic needs (clothing, groceries, hygiene items, bedding).
* Partnerships include Barrow Neurological Institute, HonorHealth and Northern Arizona University, per program summaries.

**Eligibility Requirements**
* Young people who have transitioned out of foster care; program materials describe ages 18–24, while the website's help page says ages 18–23 — confirm the current age range.
* Youth may come from anywhere in Arizona's foster-care system, but housing and services concentrate in the East Valley/Maricopa County; participants generally enter with little or no income and no stable housing.
* Ask whether a Department of Child Safety, agency or self-referral is required and what the intake assessment involves.

**Population Served**
* Young adults (about 18–24) aging out of foster care in Maricopa County, especially Mesa, Tempe and surrounding East Valley communities; program reporting notes high rates of trauma and traumatic brain injury and that participants are roughly 40% female and 60% male.

**How to Best Connect**
* Email info@foster360az.org or call 480-834-2115; office address 137 E. University Dr., Mesa, AZ 85201; website foster360.org (see "Need Help?" for youth who have transitioned from foster care).
* Ask about current openings, the intake process and whether referrals are needed; Foster360 is described on its site as an Azura Solutions Initiative.
* No walk-in hours are published; contact first to arrange next steps.

**Important Information to Know**
* Capacity is limited — program reports describe roughly 11–12 young adults housed at a time or annually, with a long-term goal of supporting at least 100 young adults; ask about waitlists.
* No cost to participants was stated in program materials; ask what is covered and what participants contribute, if anything.
* The age range differs across materials (18–23 vs. 18–24) — confirm current eligibility.
* Funding includes Mesa United Way and other community grants; services and bed availability can change, and no placement is guaranteed.

resources.description: AllThrive 365 — the nonprofit formerly known as Foundation for Senior Living (FSL) — owns and manages affordable apartment communities across Arizona, including six in the Phoenix area, for older adults, adults with disabilities, and families with limited incomes. Each community has its own age and income rules and a local manager who handles applications.
resources.hours: Not published — call 602-285-1800 or the individual community manager
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
AllThrive 365 (the organization formerly called Foundation for Senior Living / FSL) owns and manages affordable apartment communities across Arizona, including six in the Greater Phoenix area:
- Acacia Heights — 78 units, ages 62+; 615 W. Pierson St., Phoenix 85013; manager Jeff Weist, 602-767-5812, JeffW@allthrive365.org
- Spectrum Courtyard — 25 units, family housing and adults with developmental disabilities; 5330 N. 21st Ave., Phoenix 85015; Jeff Weist, 602-767-5814, JeffW@allthrive365.org
- Vianney Villas Apartments — 50 units, ages 62+; 750 S. 4th St., Avondale 85323; Sylvia Ontiveros, 623-932-2036, SylviaO@allthrive365.org
- Sweetwater Gardens Apartments — 24 units, adults 18+ with mobility impairments; 2035 E. Sweetwater Ave., Phoenix 85022; Scott Van Soest, 602-867-4549, ScottV@allthrive365.org
- Village on Roeser — 112 units, ages 55+ and households 18+; 454 E. Roeser Rd., Phoenix 85040; Elvira Lopez, 602-268-5100, ElviraL@allthrive365.org
- 29 Palms Apartments — 21 units, ages 55+ and adults with developmental disabilities; 4901 E. Holly St., Phoenix 85008; Elvira Lopez, 602-595-7901, ElviraL@allthrive365.org
The organization also runs communities outside Maricopa County (Cottonwood, Flagstaff, Holbrook, Mayer, Payson, Prescott, Prescott Valley, Show Low, Williams, Coolidge, Yuma, Tucson, Lake Havasu City, Kingman and Wickenburg — full list at allthrive365.org/housing/affordable-housing), plus a Resource Navigator program that helps older adults and caregivers find services, and home energy-efficiency help.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Eligibility varies by property and is based on income and household size; each community is limited to a specific population — ages 62+, ages 55+, adults with disabilities (developmental disabilities or mobility impairments), or family housing. Exact income limits, rents and screening requirements are not published online; the manager for the specific community can explain the criteria and current limits.

**Population Served**
Older adults (55+ and 62+ communities), adults with developmental disabilities or mobility impairments, and families and individuals with limited incomes. Six communities are in the Phoenix metro area (Maricopa County); the rest are elsewhere in Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the central office at 602-285-1800 (TTY 602-297-1844) or email info@allthrive365.org; main office: 1201 E. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85014. For a specific community, contact its manager directly using the names, phone numbers and emails listed above — managers handle applications and can explain availability, rents and paperwork. Note that "Foundation for Senior Living" and "FSL" now operate as AllThrive 365 (fsl.org redirects to allthrive365.org), so search both names when looking this up.

**Important Information to Know**
- The rebrand from Foundation for Senior Living (FSL) to AllThrive 365 took effect in April 2025 — it is the same housing program under a new name.
- These are permanent, income-restricted apartments, not emergency shelter. Waitlists, vacancy, rents and income limits can change and are not published — confirm directly with the community manager.
- No online application is listed; apply by phone or email with the manager. The website offers English and Spanish.
- Key links: allthrive365.org/housing/affordable-housing (community list); allthrive365.org (main site); fsl.org (redirects to the new site).

It takes single women 18+ and, per published listings, women with young children; stays are short (about 30 days or less) and free. Intake is by phone — call before going.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Gift of Mary Home is a small emergency shelter for women in central Phoenix, run by the Missionaries of Charity (the religious order founded by St. Mother Teresa) next to Our Lady of Fatima Parish Mission. Published shelter information lists about 10 beds for single women plus a small number of beds for women with children, free of charge, with short stays (listed as about 30 days or less).

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Women 18 and older.
- Women with children have been accepted: a 2020 community resource list says girls of any age and boys age 5 or younger; another public listing says children 5 or younger. Confirm the current age limits by phone.
- A photo ID is required.
- Space is very limited — call first to check availability.

**Population Served**
Single adult women and mothers with young children who are experiencing homelessness in Phoenix and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-254-8424 for intake and availability before going. Address: 1406 S. 17th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007 (next door to Our Lady of Fatima Parish Mission, 1418 S. 17th Ave.). Listed hours: shelter 3:30 p.m.–8:30 a.m.; office hours Monday–Friday 8:30 a.m.–3:30 p.m. If the shelter line does not answer, the parish office next door (602-254-4944; olfphx@gmail.com) may be able to relay a message.

**Important Information to Know**
- Free shelter with no website of its own. Intake details (hours, child age limits, length of stay, capacity) come from published shelter listings and community reports rather than an official page — call first and confirm everything before traveling.
- The shelter is very small, so a bed should never be assumed.
- St. Mother Teresa established Gift of Mary Home next to the parish in 1989; the Missionaries of Charity sisters still serve there, and a November 2025 community item referenced donations to the home — it is believed to be operating, but confirm current status when you call.
- One neighbor description calls the home an outreach to "poor men, women, and children," while shelter listings describe a women's shelter — confirm who can currently stay.
- Key links: shelterlist.com (Gift of Mary Women's Shelter listing); olfphx.com (Our Lady of Fatima Parish Mission, “We are the home of the Missionaries of Charity”).

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
UMOM New Day Centers builds and operates permanent, income-restricted apartment communities around the Valley through its subsidiary, Helping Hands Housing Services. Current communities include:
- La Esperanza Terrace — 3101 W. McDowell Rd., Phoenix; 96 units (1–3 bedrooms); families at or below 60% of Area Median Income; opened April 2025; community room, computer lab, fitness center, playground; computer training, financial literacy and job-seeking support for residents.
- Salamanca Square — 4439 N. 39th Ave., Phoenix; under development (groundbreaking in 2026); planned at roughly 192 units (1–4 bedrooms) for families at 50–60% AMI; not leasing yet.
- 9 South — 60 units (2–3 bedrooms), opened 2023.
- Newsom Village — 60 units (2–3 bedrooms) in south Phoenix, opened 2022.
- Bethany Crossing — Glendale; 72 family units, opened 2021.
- 19 West — north Phoenix; 54 family units, opened 2019.
- South 7th Village — south Phoenix; community for people 55+, with priority given to veterans.
- Legacy Crossing — 80 permanent affordable units across from UMOM's main campus.
- Parsons Village — 48 units of affordable and permanent supportive housing, plus employment services, a computer lab and life-skills classes.
Many communities offer on-site resident services (job readiness, financial coaching, computer classes, English-language and life-skills support). UMOM states it aims to open one new affordable community per year.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Income limits apply at every community (commonly at or below 60% of Area Median Income; newer projects at 50–60% AMI); standard rental screening (income verification, background/credit checks) is handled by the property manager.
- South 7th Village is for people 55+ (veterans priority); other communities primarily serve families and individuals.
- UMOM shelter or program participants may apply, but they receive no preference, and UMOM does not subsidize rent at its own properties.

**Population Served**
Low-income families and individuals, older adults 55+ (South 7th Village, with veterans priority), and people moving out of homelessness into permanent supportive housing (Parsons Village). Communities are in Maricopa County (Phoenix and Glendale).

**How to Best Connect**
- Apply to a specific community: all UMOM affordable communities are managed by Biltmore Properties, Inc. (main office: 2330 W. Mission Ln., Suite 10, Phoenix, AZ 85021; 602-997-0013, weekday hours). Leasing hours and waitlists vary by property — call ahead.
- Program questions: UMOM, 3333 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85008; 602-275-7852; umom.org/affordable-housing; listed office hours Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
- If you are a family in an immediate housing crisis, call the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 or 2-1-1 — the affordable communities are not crisis or shelter intake.

**Important Information to Know**
- These are permanent apartments, not emergency shelter; demand is high and waiting lists are common.
- Rents are income-restricted but not published (one project announced rents of roughly $828–$1,600 depending on unit size and income while it was under construction — confirm current figures).
- Applications go to the property manager; UMOM clients receive no preferential treatment.
- UMOM states it has built hundreds of Valley units to date (its site prints "over 1,00 units" — treat the exact total as approximate).
- Key links: umom.org/affordable-housing; umom.org/find-help; Maricopa County release on La Esperanza Terrace (maricopa.gov).

resources.description: Homeward Bound, a Phoenix nonprofit founded in 1990 to shelter families experiencing homelessness, was acquired by A New Leaf in 2024. Its campus at 2302 W. Colter St. now operates as Thunderbird Apartments — 75 affordable two-bedroom homes with optional on-site support — and A New Leaf continues serving families in crisis through the countywide Family Housing Hub.
resources.hours: Listed campus hours Mon–Fri 9 a.m.–5 p.m. (2024 fact sheet); leasing office hours not published — confirm by phone
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Thunderbird Apartments (the former Homeward Bound campus at 2302 W. Colter St.) offers 75 two-bedroom apartment homes (76 affordable units on the campus) for low-to-moderate-income households, with housing vouchers accepted and a waitlist possible depending on availability. On-site services are optional and include case management, employment guidance, financial coaching, life-skills opportunities and referrals; amenities include playgrounds, outdoor fitness, laundry, gated parking and a secure pedestrian gate. The campus also hosts the Strong Foundations Early Learning Center (licensed child care for children 0–5, serving residents and neighbors) and partner appointments with Homeless ID Project, Adelante Healthcare, Family Legal Services and Phoenix Children's Hospital, plus a residents-only food and basic-needs pantry. Homeward Bound's family shelter and transitional housing legacy continues under A New Leaf; families experiencing homelessness enter through the countywide Family Housing Hub.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Thunderbird Apartments: income qualifications for low-to-moderate-income households. Published rental criteria include household income at least twice the monthly rent (or twice the portion of rent not covered by a voucher), government photo ID, an established credit file (no minimum score), and background review — felony convictions must be more than 3 years old, no violent felony convictions within the last 5 years, no active warrants, no registered sex offenders, and no evictions in the past 12 months. Pets are allowed (maximum 2, 50 lbs or less, breed restrictions). Households generally may not exceed 2 people per bedroom plus 1.
- Family shelter: for families with children; entry is through the Family Housing Hub, and placement is not guaranteed.

**Population Served**
Families and individuals with low-to-moderate incomes (apartments), families with children experiencing homelessness (shelter/transitional services), and children ages 0–5 (early learning center). Services are based in Phoenix and serve the greater Valley/Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
- Apartments: call the leasing office at 602-899-8089 (AZ Property Brokerage) or email thunderbirdapts@azpropertybrokerage.com; submit an application and meet income/screening criteria; waitlists possible. Address: 2302 W. Colter St., Phoenix, AZ 85015.
- Family shelter: Family Housing Hub — 602-595-8700 or 2-1-1 / 877-211-8661; the hub is on the UMOM campus at 3333 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix. Placement is not guaranteed.
- Child care: hbreception@turnanewleaf.org or 602-374-8770.
- General housing help: housing@turnanewleaf.org; A New Leaf main office: 868 E. University Dr., Mesa, AZ 85203; 480-969-4024.

**Important Information to Know**
- Homeward Bound was acquired by A New Leaf in 2024; the old homewardboundaz.org website now redirects to A New Leaf, and the campus is presented as Thunderbird Apartments — same location and services, new branding. When a family says "Homeward Bound," this is the current operation.
- Costs: published rental criteria state that deposits and fees may be required as little as 24 hours after acceptance — ask what is required before applying.
- Federal subaward records show a December 2024 City of Mesa CDBG award to Homeward Bound ($65,300) for housing, case management, employment and navigation services for 70 people; current City of Mesa funding status was not confirmed online during this check, so treat Mesa contracting details as unverified.
- Key links: turnanewleaf.org (Thunderbird Apartments page and 2026 fact sheets); turnanewleaf.org/homeward-bound-merger.

resources.description: House of Miracles, Inc. (HOMI) is a Phoenix-based nonprofit that helps people who are unhoused or low-income find stable, supportive housing and connects them with food, clothing, hygiene supplies, mental-health and substance-use support, and job-readiness help. HOMI works as a resource and referral agency - it assists clients in locating transitional and supportive housing rather than advertising its own housing units.
resources.hours: Not published - call or email first; no walk-in hours are posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
HOMI helps individuals and families locate transitional and supportive housing - its website says it assists people in finding stable, safe, and supportive living arrangements - and its Community Cares/Contexture referral program connects clients to affordable and supportive housing, workforce and job-readiness assistance, clothing, nutrition assistance, and hygiene supplies. HOMI also offers food-assistance referrals around Maricopa County, SNAP outreach and application help, mental-health and substance-use counseling and education, employment readiness training, mentoring and life coaching, financial and nutrition workshops, and youth programs. Once someone becomes a client, HOMI completes an entrance assessment and matches services to their needs.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No formal eligibility rules are published. HOMI says it serves people facing barriers such as eviction history, poor credit, mental illness, substance use, low but sustainable income, and criminal convictions, and it receives daily social-service referrals from partner agencies through Unite Us/Community Cares. For housing assistance, contact HOMI to ask what it can offer in your situation and whether a partner-agency referral is needed.

**Population Served**
People who are unhoused or at risk of homelessness and low-income individuals and families in Maricopa County. HOMI states its programs reach seniors, teens, low-income families, unhoused people, people with mental-health or substance-use conditions, and people connected to the criminal justice system; it also describes a history of serving men and women in early recovery from drugs and alcohol and people transitioning from homelessness.

**How to Best Connect**
Call (623) 203-7381 or email admin@houseofmiraclesinc.com (alternate email: homihouse2020@gmail.com) to ask about housing navigation and the Community Cares/Contexture program. Partner agencies can refer clients through Unite Us/Community Cares. No walk-in hours are posted, so call or email first; if a case manager at another agency already works with the household, ask them to send a referral.

**Important Information to Know**
HOMI operates as a navigation and referral service rather than a confirmed housing provider - it is not clear whether HOMI directly leases or operates housing units, so ask exactly what housing it can connect you to and how long that may take. No fees or costs are published; confirm any costs directly. The website does not list walk-in hours; a federal NPI registration lists an office at 1951 W. Camelback Rd., Suite 255, Phoenix - confirm by phone before visiting. HOMI is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN 86-1009934) and states it is retired-veteran operated. HOMI does not advertise emergency shelter; for immediate shelter needs call 2-1-1 (1-877-211-8661).

resources.description: House of Refuge is a faith-based nonprofit in southeast Mesa that provides transitional housing for families with children who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or fleeing domestic violence. Families live in one of 88 furnished two-bedroom homes on a 20-acre neighborhood and receive case management, employment and education support, and children's programs while they work toward stable housing.
resources.hours: Administrative office: Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-4 p.m. Housing intake is by phone/email/inquiry form; the program is not an emergency shelter - for immediate shelter call 211 (1-877-211-8661).
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Furnished transitional housing in two-bedroom homes (88 homes on a 20-acre neighborhood in southeast Mesa) plus wrap-around services: an assigned case manager and individualized case plan, a housing plan for the move to permanent housing, employment and education support through an on-site Employment & Education Center, life-skills, financial-literacy and nutrition classes, after-school programming for children 5-11, a teen center for ages 12-17, and access to a donation center for clothing, furniture and household items plus a certified food bank. Participants sign a lease and pay $400 per month with utilities included; the program describes itself as a transitional housing work program with a roughly year-long stay.

**Eligibility Requirements**
You must be deemed homeless, have received an eviction notice, or be fleeing domestic violence; currently reside in Arizona; have verifiable income of at least $1,170 per month (examples: pay stubs, SSI, child support, spousal maintenance - cash jobs are not accepted) and maintain it throughout the stay; pass a urine drug test and a background check (no sex-offense charges or convictions); be drug- and alcohol-free; have an adult 18 or older to sign the lease; and have custody of at least one minor child living with you or be in your third trimester of pregnancy. If income at move-in is not from employment, you must agree to gain employment within 45 days. Eligibility does not guarantee acceptance.

**Population Served**
Families with at least one minor child and pregnant women in their third trimester who are homeless, at risk of homelessness, or fleeing domestic violence. House of Refuge reports serving about 160 families (514 individuals) in a recent year, with children making up roughly 62% of residents.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-988-9242 or email info@houseofrefuge.org. When the program has openings, the Housing Inquiry Form is posted on the Need Housing page at houseofrefuge.org/need-housing/ - the page says to check back often. Administrative/mailing office: 6935 E. Williams Field Rd., Mesa, AZ 85212; the housing neighborhood is in southeast Mesa. House of Refuge does not offer emergency or immediate shelter - if you need shelter right away, dial 211 (1-877-211-8661).

**Important Information to Know**
Costs: $400 per month rent (utilities included); new residents have also been required since January 1, 2025 to pay a $200 security deposit and the last month's rent ($400) at move-in. The inquiry form is only available when the program has openings, so it may not be possible to apply at any given time - call to ask about openings and timing. The program requires work, minimum income, sobriety, background and drug screening, Arizona residency, and custody of a minor child (or third-trimester pregnancy). Eligibility does not guarantee acceptance, and there may be wait times. The program is faith-based and located in Mesa.

resources.description: The Housing Authority of Maricopa County (HAMC) is the public housing agency for much of unincorporated Maricopa County outside Phoenix, Glendale, Scottsdale, Tempe, Chandler, and most of Mesa. HAMC administers Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8), project-based vouchers, and referral-based special vouchers - HUD-VASH for homeless veterans, Mainstream vouchers for adults with disabilities, and Family Unification Program vouchers - and its federal Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) program is winding down with the wait list closed.
resources.hours: Office hours are generally Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m.; call 602-744-4500 to confirm. Wait-list status changes - check HAMC's Wait List Schedule.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rental assistance for low-income households: tenant-based Housing Choice Vouchers (Section 8) used to rent privately owned housing; project-based vouchers tied to specific HAMC properties; and special voucher programs filled by referral - HUD-VASH (rental assistance plus VA case management for homeless veterans), Mainstream vouchers (households that include a non-elderly person with disabilities, age 18-61), and Family Unification Program vouchers (families whose children are at risk of out-of-home placement, and eligible young adults 18-24 leaving foster care). The Emergency Housing Voucher (EHV) program - which historically took referrals through the Maricopa Continuum of Care for people who were homeless, at risk of homelessness, fleeing domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking or human trafficking, or recently homeless - is winding down as federal funding ends, and its list is closed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
HCV: very low-income households under HUD limits (HAMC posts current income limits); households provide Social Security numbers (if applicable), birth dates, and income information; at least one household member must have legal residency. A felony is not an automatic disqualification (it depends on the conviction and how long ago it occurred), but registered sex offenders are ineligible, as are people ever convicted of manufacturing or producing methamphetamine on federally assisted housing premises. Referral programs have their own criteria (for example, HUD-VASH requires homeless-veteran status verified through the VA). Geography matters: HAMC's voucher jurisdiction excludes Phoenix, Glendale, Scottsdale, Tempe, Chandler and most of Mesa - within Mesa, only county islands in East Mesa (south and east of Power Road) are in HAMC's area; check the boundary map at geo.azmag.gov/maps/hamc.

**Population Served**
Very low-income households; people experiencing or at risk of homelessness (through coordinated-entry referral programs); homeless veterans (HUD-VASH); non-elderly adults with disabilities (Mainstream); families involved with child welfare and young adults leaving foster care (Family Unification Program); and current EHV families transitioning into the HCV program as EHV winds down.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 602-744-4500 or email info@maricopahousing.org; office: 8910 N. 78th Ave., Building D, Peoria, AZ 85345 (generally Monday-Friday, 8 a.m.-5 p.m.). Check HAMC's Wait List Schedule on maricopahousing.org for which lists are open - as of September 15, 2026: EHV closed; Section 8/HCV closed (closed since August 25, 2023); Family Unification, Mainstream and HUD-VASH open by referral only; some property/project-based lists open at times. When the HCV list opens, HAMC announces it publicly in advance and takes applications through its online applicant portal - watch maricopahousing.org/news and the Wait List Schedule. For coordinated-entry referrals: families with children call the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700; single adults can call 2-1-1 (1-877-211-8661) for the nearest coordinated entry point; homeless veterans can contact the VA Community Resource & Referral Center at 602-248-6040.

**Important Information to Know**
EHV is not open to new applicants: HAMC's schedule lists EHV as closed and HAMC policy describes the program winding down as federal funds end, with current EHV families transitioned into the HCV program. The Section 8/HCV list is also closed and opens only when HAMC announces an opening - no application is accepted while it is closed, and waits can take years. Voucher households generally pay about 30% of adjusted income toward rent; confirm details with HAMC. No application fees are stated by HAMC; ask if any costs apply. HAMC's jurisdiction excludes Phoenix, Glendale, Scottsdale, Tempe, Chandler and most of Mesa - verify the specific address before applying, and ask HAMC or 2-1-1 which housing authority covers your address. HAMC also owns and manages affordable apartment communities with their own wait lists - ask about those as an alternative.

resources.description: Keys to Change (formerly Human Services Campus) operates Key Campus, a 13-acre downtown Phoenix hub at 12th Avenue and Madison for single adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. The Brian Garcia Welcome Center is the walk-up entry point for diversion, assessment, and shelter referrals; the campus includes the 600-bed CASS Single Adult Shelter, the 95-bed Respiro shelter run by Keys to Change, and a remaining St. Vincent de Paul overflow space - a reduced, funding-dependent version of the pandemic-era nightly overflow - plus meals, health care, ID, mail, showers, storage, employment and housing-match services. The campus shelters nearly 900 people per night.
resources.hours: Brian Garcia Welcome Center: open 24 hours a day. Key Campus is operating 24/7 through September 30, 2026 (heat relief); call 602-883-4509 to confirm timing and shelter availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency shelter access for single adults. Shelter referrals are made through the Brian Garcia Welcome Center, which provides diversion services, vulnerability screenings, and shelter placement to the campus's shelter spaces: the 600-bed CASS Single Adult Shelter, the 95-bed Respiro emergency shelter (operated by Keys to Change, with housing navigation), and a remaining St. Vincent de Paul overflow space - the last remnant of the nightly overflow mats that began during the pandemic. The campus is also a one-stop service hub with 13 partner organizations: meals, mail service, ID and birth-certificate replacement, showers, safe storage, medical and dental care, mental-health and substance-use services, state benefits (AHCCCS/SNAP), SSI/Social Security advocacy, employment help, legal services and homeless court, pet services, heat relief, and coordinated entry/housing-match services that connect people to housing and vouchers.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Key Campus shelters and serves single adults (people without minor children) who are experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. Shelter placement follows screening and referral at the Welcome Center and depends on bed availability - the campus says its shelters are full most nights and people are turned away when capacity is reached. Families with children are served separately through the Family Housing Hub (602-595-8700); youth ages 12-17 should call the 24/7 youth hotline (602-841-5799); veterans can use the VA Community Resource & Referral Center at 1500 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 106 (602-248-6040).

**Population Served**
Single adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. Keys to Change says it works with close to 14,000 individuals a year and the campus serves more than 1,000 people daily, whether they are unsheltered or staying in shelter.

**How to Best Connect**
Go in person to the Brian Garcia Welcome Center on Key Campus (204 S. 12th Ave., Phoenix - at 12th Avenue and Madison; the Welcome Center is also listed at 206 S. 12th Ave.) or call 602-883-4509. The Welcome Center is described as open 24 hours a day; campus operations were extended to 24/7 through September 30, 2026 for heat relief. Call first to confirm timing and shelter availability. For a coordinated-entry point closer to home, call 2-1-1 (1-877-211-8661). Campus main line: 602-229-5155; general office: 602-282-0853. Keys to Change also hosts Project Connect pop-up resource events several times a year around the Valley.

**Important Information to Know**
The nightly overflow shelter has shrunk significantly: the pandemic-era overflow once added about 280 mats in two spaces; the Lodestar Day Resource Center overflow closed June 1, 2025, and the remaining St. Vincent de Paul dining-room overflow was reported at about 170 mats in 2025 and was still counted among the campus's three shelter spaces in spring 2026. Funding for overflow remains fragile, and shelter capacity changes - call before going. Older guides that say to arrive by 5:30 p.m. for an overflow mat may be outdated; ask the Welcome Center how evening placement works. Shelters are frequently full, and no cost information is published for shelter entry - ask staff whether any fees apply. The campus is in downtown Phoenix, not Mesa, and serves people from across Maricopa County, so plan transportation if traveling from the East Valley. Some older listings give a W. Jackson St. address for this campus; the current official address is 204 S. 12th Ave.

resources.hours: Open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; current guidance is to visit 7am–11pm to begin an assessment and plan
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
In-person help for single adults experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness in Maricopa County: diversion (short- and long-term housing planning), vulnerability screening and assessment, shelter referrals, and Coordinated Entry into housing. The Welcome Center is the lead access point for single-adult Coordinated Entry, and the Keys to Change Housing Match team manages the county's By-Name List used to prioritize people for housing and vouchers. Staff also connect clients to Key Campus services, including replacement ID and birth certificates, mail, storage, showers, medical and dental care, mental health and substance use services, DES state benefits, Social Security (SOAR) help, employment services, legal help and Homeless Court, meals, and pet services.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Single adults 18 and older who are experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County; Keys to Change also describes its services as open to single adults at risk of homelessness. No documents are required to begin and there is no fee. Staff complete diversion and screening to determine next steps.

**Population Served**
Single adults 18+ across Maricopa County, including Mesa residents, among them people with disabilities, medical conditions, and other high needs. Services are listed as available in English and Spanish on the 2-1-1 record. Families with children, youth under 18, veterans, and domestic-violence survivors have separate official routes (see Important Information to Know).

**How to Best Connect**
Walk in to the Brian Garcia Welcome Center at 206 S. 12th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007, on Key Campus — open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with current guidance to visit any time from 7am–11pm to begin an assessment and create a plan. Call ahead: 602-883-4509. Key Campus main line: 602-229-5155. No appointment is needed. From Mesa or elsewhere in the county, call 2-1-1 (1-877-211-8661) to find the nearest Maricopa County Coordinated Entry access point. Help is delivered in person; the phone line is for calling ahead, not for completing intake.

**Important Information to Know**
Free; no documents required to start. A shelter bed or housing placement is not guaranteed — resources are limited and demand is high, so a referral starts a process that may include waiting. Phone numbers in circulation differ: the official call-ahead number is 602-883-4509, the campus main line is 602-229-5155, and some older listings show 602-299-5155 — use the official numbers. Hours nuance: the Welcome Center is open 24/7, while current guidance says assessment visits run 7am–11pm. Other official routes: families with children — Family Housing Hub, 602-595-8700 (waiting list; TDD 602-759-1896); youth 12–17 — 24/7 Youth Hotline, 602-841-5799; veterans — VA Community Resource and Referral Center, 1500 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 106, 602-248-6040, Mon–Fri 7:30am–4:30pm (national line: 1-877-424-3838); domestic violence — 24/7 DV Centralized Screening Line, 480-890-3039. The Welcome Center also hosts part-time veteran services through the Traumatic Brain Injury Alliance. If the phone mailbox is full, keep calling or visit in person.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Respiro is a 95-bed emergency shelter on Key Campus operated by Keys to Change (opened March 2022; 6,300-square-foot structure). Guests can stay in the shelter 24/7, not just overnight. The co-ed space has air conditioning, beds, showers, restrooms, storage for belongings, vending machines, and an outdoor patio. Pets, service animals, and emotional support animals are allowed, and Key Campus has a designated dog run plus pet services through the Arizona Pet Project. On-site housing navigation staff work with guests toward housing, and the campus provides access to ID replacement, health and dental care, state benefits, meals, showers, and more.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults experiencing homelessness who come through the single-adult Coordinated Entry process — placement starts at the Brian Garcia Welcome Center on the same campus, which provides diversion, screening, and shelter referrals. No shelter fee is listed; confirm any costs at intake. Pet owners are welcome; confirm current pet requirements when applying.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County who are referred through Coordinated Entry, including pet owners. The shelter is co-ed and has 95 beds.

**How to Best Connect**
Go to the Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Ave., Phoenix (Key Campus) — open 24 hours a day; visit from 7am–11pm to begin an assessment. Call ahead: 602-883-4509; Key Campus main line: 602-229-5155. Respiro has no separate public intake line — ask for it by name at the Welcome Center. From Mesa, you can call 2-1-1 to find the nearest Coordinated Entry point, but Respiro is located on Key Campus in Phoenix.

**Important Information to Know**
Beds are limited: Respiro has operated at or near full capacity since it opened, so placement is not guaranteed and depends on shelter availability and Coordinated Entry priority. The shelter permits pets and service/emotional support animals and lets guests remain on site during the day — confirm current pet rules, storage limits, and the referral flow with Keys to Change. Published details about capacity and pet policies can become dated, so verify current conditions at intake rather than relying on secondhand information.

resources.description: Tempe-based program providing up to 90 days of complete care — shelter, food, medical care, and enrichment — for dogs and cats whose owners in Arizona are in crisis (homelessness, eviction, domestic violence, medical treatment, foreclosure, financial hardship). Keeps pets safe so owners can seek shelter, treatment, or housing and then be reunited; application required; high demand.
resources.hours: Temporary Care Program office: Tuesday–Saturday, 10am–5:30pm; urgent-case emails reviewed daily (responses within 48 hours)
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Temporary Care Program: up to 90 days (sometimes up to 120 days) of complete care for dogs and cats whose owners are in crisis — shelter, food, medical care, and enrichment — with the goal of reuniting pets with their families afterward. Lost Our Home also runs a pet food bank (Animeals on Wheels), a domestic-violence program that partners with local DV shelters (up to 120 days of free pet care for their clients), rescue and adoption for abandoned or surrendered pets, and lifetime-care assistance. For owners facing homelessness, eviction, or housing that will not allow pets, this program keeps the animal safe while the owner seeks shelter, treatment, or housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Arizona residents facing a qualifying crisis: eviction, homelessness, domestic violence, medical treatment or rehabilitation, foreclosure, financial hardship, veteran/disabled veteran circumstances, or other crises. Pets must be spayed/neutered (before entering the program or during it) and meet health requirements — dogs: rabies, distemper/parvo (DA2PPv), and bordetella vaccinations plus proof of spay/neuter; cats: FVRCP vaccination, negative FeLV/FIV test, plus proof of spay/neuter. Lost Our Home can help with missing vaccinations. Applicants must respond within 48 hours when contacted, and services are not offered out of state.

**Population Served**
Arizona families and individuals in the Phoenix metro area (including Tempe and Mesa) whose pets need temporary care during a personal crisis; program materials describe it as the most comprehensive temporary pet care program in the Valley. Listed examples include people experiencing eviction or homelessness, domestic-violence survivors, and people entering hospital or rehabilitation care. Spanish-language program pages ("Cuidado Temporal") are available.

**How to Best Connect**
Apply online with the Temporary Care Application at https://new.shelterluv.com/form/community/LOH/20738-temporary-care-program, or call the Temporary Care Program office at 602-445-7391, Tuesday–Saturday, 10am–5:30pm (main line: 602-445-7387). Urgent cases: complete the application, then email TCP@lostourhome.org with "TCP Urgent" in the subject line, including your name, your pet's names, and a brief statement of urgency — urgent cases are reviewed daily and answered within 48 hours. The shelter is at 2323 S. Hardy Drive, Tempe, AZ 85282.

**Important Information to Know**
No fee is mentioned in program materials and news reporting describes the service as free (food and medical costs covered) — confirm any costs when you apply. Demand is high and the program may not be able to help immediately; if you do not respond to staff within 48 hours, your application moves to the next person. The standard stay is up to 90 days (some cases, including domestic-violence clients, extend to 120), and the goal is reunification with your pet. Vaccination and spay/neuter requirements apply; pets cannot remain intact. This program cares for pets — it does not provide human housing or shelter; it removes the pet barrier while you seek housing, shelter, or treatment.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Rotating overnight emergency lodging for people experiencing homelessness in the Mesa area: participating faith congregations take turns hosting guests overnight, and the broader East Valley I-HELP model includes evening and morning meals, case management, referrals to community resources, bus passes, mobile shower access, and medical referrals. New guests complete a pre-screening interview; exact services for the Mesa program could not be confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Unconfirmed and conflicting: a 2024 directory listing describes the Lutheran Social Services I-HELP Mesa program as serving women without children who are experiencing homelessness (and not accepting sex offenders or animals, including service animals), while other community descriptions of Mesa I-HELP describe screened adults expected to be clean, sober, and actively seeking employment. All I-HELP listings require a pre-screening interview and a call to check bed availability before entering. Confirm current eligibility before referring anyone.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Mesa and the East Valley; the reported population differs by source — one listing says women without children, while other descriptions suggest mixed adults. Confirm who is currently served.

**How to Best Connect**
Call to confirm the program and check bed availability, then complete the required pre-screening interview. Reported contact routes: 480-684-0645 (Lutheran Social Services of the Southwest I-HELP Mesa — intake by phone Monday–Thursday, 8am–noon; leave a message or text if no answer); 480-396-3795 (county shelter list for LSS I-HELP Mesa/Northwest/Southwest); 480-654-4539 (reported Mesa I-HELP number). Dialing 2-1-1 (1-877-211-8661) is the most reliable way to confirm the current operator and intake. A listed office address is 2502 E. University Ave., Ste. 125, Phoenix, AZ 85034; host sites rotate among Mesa congregations (an I-HELP host has been listed at 5946 E. University Dr., Mesa).

**Important Information to Know**
This lead is unresolved: sources disagree about who currently operates the Mesa I-HELP program (Lutheran Social Services of the Southwest vs. AZCEND contacts) and about who is eligible (women without children vs. all adults), and the available information dates from 2021–2024. Reported phone numbers conflict, so confirm the current number before a client calls. A claim that I-HELP includes motel vouchers and move-in/storage help comes from a third-party aggregator and is unverified — do not promise it. I-HELP programs in other cities (for example, AZCEND's I-HELP in Chandler) are separate programs run by different agencies, which adds to the confusion. Because of these conflicts, verify the current operator, eligibility, and intake route before referring; until then, treat this as a lead for follow-up rather than a confirmed bed.

resources.description: Maggie's Place is a Phoenix-based nonprofit operating maternity homes across the Valley for women who are homeless and pregnant. The Hannah House is its Mesa home, and a five-bedroom "bunkhouse" on the same property (opened 2023) adds more safe shelter for expecting women. The program provides a stable home during pregnancy and after birth, plus coaching and support services. Intake is centralized through one intake specialist, there is no listed fee, and capacity is limited, so call early.
resources.hours: Intake by phone (messages returned in order); listed weekday office hours approx. 9 a.m.-5 p.m. - confirm before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Emergency shelter and a stable home for women who are homeless and pregnant at The Hannah House in Mesa, including a separate five-bedroom "bunkhouse" on the same property that adds more safe nights of shelter for expecting women.
- Wraparound support: family coaching and case management, parenting and child-development programs, employment assistance, nutrition and infant supplies, health and wellness programs, and help connecting to prenatal care and community resources; alumnae support continues after moms leave.
- Maggie's Place operates several maternity homes across the Valley; women are placed where space is available, so openings at The Hannah House vary.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Must be homeless and pregnant, age 18 or older, free from immediate physical danger, without other children in her immediate care, and willing to live in community.
- A 2-1-1 Arizona listing adds: substance-free for at least 30 days, no active warrants, and openness to sharing a room.
- Bring proof of pregnancy to the intake meeting.

**Population Served**
- Pregnant women experiencing homelessness (18 and older) and, after birth, mothers with their babies. 2-1-1 lists a statewide service area and classifies the program as a maternity home.
- The Hannah House serves a small number of women and children each year (about 31 recently), and program materials say demand exceeds capacity.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call the intake specialist at 602-246-3724. If no one answers, leave a message; calls are returned in the order received.
- The next step is an interview at the Family Success Center, 4001 N. 30th St., Phoenix, AZ 85016. The process can take from one day to a few weeks depending on availability.
- If you need immediate emergency housing, call 2-1-1. Main line: 602-262-5555; website: maggiesplace.org. A Spanish-language mom portal is available online; confirm Spanish-language intake support when calling.
- Ask about current openings at The Hannah House (Mesa) versus other Maggie's Place homes.

**Important Information to Know**
- No fee is listed for services.
- Stay length: Maggie's Place describes support through "baby's first year," while its 2-1-1 listing says women can stay until the baby is 9 months old - confirm the current length at intake.
- Office hours: weekday hours (about 9 a.m.-5 p.m.) are listed, but one listing shows Wednesday closed - call before visiting.
- The shelter location is confidential and shared during intake.
- The City of Mesa has supported The Hannah House through grant pass-through funding and describes the shelter as serving Mesa residents; this does not guarantee eligibility or a bed.

resources.resolutionReason: Retained as usable. Live Maggie's Place pages confirm identity, centralized intake (602-246-3724), qualifications for The Hannah House, and the Mesa home's five-bedroom bunkhouse addition (2023) for expecting women experiencing homelessness; the 2-1-1 record (last assured 03/01/2026) corroborates eligibility details, no fee and stay length; a 2024 City of Mesa report documents city-supported emergency shelter for homeless mothers serving Mesa residents. Stated limits: stay length (9 months vs. 'baby's first year') and office-hour variation; capacity is limited and demand exceeds it.

resources.description: MANA (Marines, Army, Navy, Air Force) House is a transitional housing program operated by Catholic Charities in Phoenix for veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Veterans live in a supportive program with an assigned case manager and a housing plan, plus employment, benefits and basic-needs services on site. Admission is only through a referral from the Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center (CRRC). Capacity is described as up to 70 veterans, and no fee is listed.
resources.hours: Administration listed Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-4 p.m.; facility staffed 24 hours. Call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Transitional housing for veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness, with an assigned case manager who helps build a plan to return to stable, permanent housing.
- On-site services: career counseling, job search, resume development, job placement and interview readiness in the Veterans Resource Center; help enrolling in VA, Social Security and DES benefits; guidance getting a DD-214 and filing VA claims; help finding permanent affordable housing; bus passes; transportation to and from the VA hospital; computer access; full kitchen and dining room; laundry and showers.
- Information about and referrals to other community resources.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Must be a veteran (the name stands for Marines, Army, Navy, Air Force).
- Only accepts referrals from the Phoenix VA Community Resource & Referral Center (CRRC) - admission is not arranged by contacting MANA House directly.
- A 2-1-1 listing describes eligibility as male veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless and notes discharge criteria may apply; women veterans and anyone with questions about discharge status should ask the CRRC what is possible.
- Contact the provider to confirm required documents.

**Population Served**
- U.S. military veterans experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness; capacity is described as up to 70 veterans.
- The 2-1-1 listing specifies male veterans; 2-1-1 lists all Arizona ZIP codes as the service area.

**How to Best Connect**
- Step 1 - Start at the Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center (CRRC): 1500 E. Thomas Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85014; 602-248-6040; Monday-Friday about 7:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Ask for a MANA House referral.
- Step 2 - Questions about the program: call MANA House at 602-254-6785; 2422 W. Holly St., Phoenix, AZ 85009. Administrative hours: Monday-Friday 8 a.m.-4 p.m.; the facility is staffed 24 hours. Call before visiting.
- More information: manahouseaz.org/get-help/mana-house.

**Important Information to Know**
- A CRRC referral is required; there is no walk-in admission.
- No fee is listed (2-1-1: "Fees: none").
- Bed availability is not published; ask the CRRC about current openings - eligibility does not guarantee a place.
- Details can change: the 2-1-1 listing was last assured 02/01/2026; confirm hours and documents by phone.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Official countywide list of Coordinated Entry access points - places where a person experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County can complete an initial interview, be connected to appropriate resources, and work on a housing plan with shelter and housing options.
- Mesa access points listed: A New Leaf - East Valley Men's Center (men), 2345 N. Country Club Dr., (480) 610-6722, Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-3 p.m.; COPA Health - Paz de Cristo, 424 W. Broadway Rd., (480) 464-2370, Mon-Fri 10 a.m.-3 p.m.
- Other entry routes in the list: single adults - Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Ave., Phoenix, (602) 229-5155; families - Family Housing Hub (call 2-1-1; the County also lists 602-595-8700); veterans - VA Community Resource & Referral Center, (602) 248-6040; single women - Halle Women's Center, (602) 362-5833; medically vulnerable - Circle the City, (602) 516-6825; plus youth, Native American, HIV and outreach points.
- It is a navigation/referral list, not a housing provider: the actual assessment and services happen at each access point.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Open to people experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County; each access point serves specific populations (single adults, families, veterans, youth, women, etc.), so use the point that matches the situation.
- No cost to use an access point. Coordinated Entry prioritizes by assessed need; completing the process does not guarantee housing or a housing voucher.

**Population Served**
- People experiencing homelessness across Maricopa County: single adults, families with children, youth (12-24), veterans, single women without children, Native American adults and youth, people who are medically vulnerable, people living with HIV/AIDS, and domestic violence survivors through specialized lines.

**How to Best Connect**
- Use the access point for the situation: Mesa - East Valley Men's Center (480-610-6722) or Paz de Cristo (480-464-2370); singles - Brian Garcia Welcome Center (602-229-5155); families - 2-1-1 / Family Housing Hub (602-595-8700); veterans - CRRC (602-248-6040); youth 12-17 - Safe Place (602-841-5799); domestic violence - SAFEDVS 24-hour line (480-890-3039).
- Call before going to confirm hours; some points are open 24/7 and others have limited daytime hours, and some sites require a phone or online pre-screen before a bed is offered.
- The current list and companion pages are linked from maricopacoc.org/get-help and maricopa.gov "Help with Homelessness" (maricopa.gov/5917). If a number does not connect, dial 2-1-1.

**Important Information to Know**
- This is a referral/navigation list, not a housing provider; the list itself states the process does not guarantee housing or a voucher.
- The list's revision date is unclear and some entries may be dated - confirm locations and hours by phone before sending anyone.
- Free to use. 2-1-1 also helps with rent and utility assistance and routes families to the Family Housing Hub.
- The CoC's Get Help page also links a seasonal heat-relief map for cooling, respite and hydration sites.

resources.description: The official Maricopa County “Help with Homelessness” page for the region's coordinated entry system. It routes people experiencing homelessness (or those helping them) to the right front-door access point by population — domestic-violence survivors, single adults, families, veterans and youth 12–17 — with direct phone numbers and locations, plus 2-1-1 as a general fallback. Use it to get a client into the correct intake line for shelter and support services in Maricopa County, including Mesa.
resources.hours: Domestic-violence crisis line: 24 hours. Brian Garcia Welcome Center: open 24/7. Other entry lines — call to confirm hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Maricopa County's coordinated entry routing: the page identifies the correct shelter/support-services access point by population and gives the direct phone number or location for each — domestic-violence survivors, single adults 18+, families, veterans and youth ages 12–17. It also lists Maricopa.gov/ApplyforHelp and 2-1-1 as general fallbacks. Coordinated entry for the county is run through the Key Campus (Housing Match team on behalf of Maricopa County).

**Eligibility Requirements**

There is no application on the page itself; each entry point screens for its own programs and checks current availability. Call the line that matches the household: single adults 18+ without children, families, veterans, or youth 12–17. Anyone fleeing domestic violence can use the 24-hour crisis line. Contacting an entry point starts an assessment — it does not guarantee a shelter bed or housing.

**Population Served**

People experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Maricopa County, including Mesa: domestic violence survivors; single adults 18 and older; families; veterans; and youth ages 12–17.

**How to Best Connect**

- Domestic violence: 24-hour SAFEDVS crisis line 480-890-3039 or toll-free 844-723-3387; or use the “Chat Live” option with A New Leaf.
- Single adults: Brian Garcia Welcome Center at the Key Campus, 204 S. 12th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007 (open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week); call 602-229-5155.
- Families: Family Housing Hub, 3307 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix; call 602-595-8700 (walk-in has been available on weekdays — confirm current hours).
- Veterans: Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center, 1500 E. Thomas Rd., Phoenix; call 602-248-6040.
- Youth (12–17): text “Safe” plus your address to 44357, or call 602-841-5799; stationary Safe Place sites include QuikTrip stores, libraries, fire stations, transit stops and some businesses.
- Not sure who to call: dial 2-1-1 or visit 211.org.

**Important Information to Know**

- No fee is charged to call these lines or complete an assessment; each program has its own rules.
- Phone numbers, addresses and hours can change; confirm before sending someone. (Some county listings show the welcome center as 206 S. 12th Ave.; the Key Campus address is 204 S. 12th Ave. — same campus at 12th Ave. and Madison.)
- Expect an assessment and possible waitlists rather than immediate placement.
- The page itself does not take applications — each number connects you straight to the intake provider.

resources.description: Maricopa County's street-outreach program for people experiencing homelessness in unincorporated areas and targeted communities. Outreach teams connect people to housing, shelter, health services, benefits, substance-use help and case management, and the public can file a request for an outreach visit. Note: Mesa, Phoenix, Chandler, Scottsdale and Glendale are outside its coverage — callers there are directed to 2-1-1.
resources.hours: No published hours; outreach teams are dispatched after a request is submitted — call to confirm follow-up timing.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Outreach teams go into targeted communities and unincorporated Maricopa County where people experiencing homelessness are known to gather, working alongside neighbors, businesses, service agencies and law enforcement. Support includes housing, food and benefit programs, mental and physical health services, substance-use help, case management, transportation, employment and long-term care. Teams assess each situation and refer to services that may include temporary and permanent housing and shelter placement; the public can initiate a request for service and an outreach team is dispatched.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Serves people experiencing homelessness within the program's coverage area: unincorporated Maricopa County plus targeted areas of Anthem, Apache Junction, Arlington, Avondale, Buckeye, Carefree, Cave Creek, Citrus Park, El Mirage, Fountain Hills, Gila Bend, Gilbert, Goodyear, Guadalupe, Litchfield Park, New River, Peoria, Queen Creek, Rio Verde, Sun City, Sun City West, Sun Lakes, Surprise, Tolleson, Tonopah, Waddell, Wickenburg, Wittman and Youngtown. Mesa, Phoenix, Chandler, Scottsdale and Glendale are NOT covered — people in those cities are directed to 2-1-1 or 211.org. No other eligibility rules are published.

**Population Served**

People experiencing homelessness or facing a housing crisis in the coverage area listed above.

**How to Best Connect**

- Request outreach for someone in the coverage area through the “request for service” form linked from the program page, or call Maricopa County Human Services at 602-506-0589.
- In Mesa or another excluded city: call 2-1-1 or visit 211.org for local services.
- For emergency shelter: call 2-1-1 or go to the Brian Garcia Welcome Center at the Key Campus, 204 S. 12th Ave., Phoenix (open 24/7).

**Important Information to Know**

- The program is county-funded; no fees are published for outreach services.
- It is outreach and navigation, not a shelter itself — teams refer into shelter, housing, treatment and benefit programs, where availability and program rules apply.
- Coverage excludes Mesa: county materials direct Mesa residents to 2-1-1.
- History note: older county announcements (2017–2019) described “Hand in Hand” as a jail-to-community effort connecting justice-involved people to supportive housing and services on release. The county's current program under this name is street outreach, and no current public information describes a jail-based partnership. For reentry-specific housing help, ask Maricopa County Human Services at 602-506-0589.

The jail-to-community framing from earlier materials is not reflected in current pages and is flagged in the record; Mesa is outside coverage, so the resource is retained as a reserve option for covered Maricopa County areas.

resources.description: Mesa's emergency shelter / temporary-housing program for residents experiencing homelessness: leased hotel rooms at the Windermere Hotel in northeast Mesa (65 rooms / 111 beds) with 24/7 staffing, case management, meals and a housing plan (generally up to 90 days). Admission is by referral only — no walk-up or drop-in. In 2026 the city selected Mercy House as the new service provider for day-to-day operations (previously Community Bridges, Inc.), and decided to keep the program at the Windermere rather than move it to the city-owned Sunaire Hotel.
resources.hours: Year-round; closed campus with 24/7 oversight. Mesa Homeless Resource Line hours vary — call to confirm.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Mesa's emergency shelter/temporary-housing program: leased hotel rooms at the Windermere Hotel in northeast Mesa (65 rooms / 111 beds), with meals, 24/7 on-site oversight, case management, a housing stability plan and connections to mental-health and substance-use treatment, medical care, employment services, schools for children, and longer-term housing. Stays are generally up to 90 days and depend on progress on the housing plan and following program rules (curfew, room checks, zero-tolerance drug policy, closed campus). The city pairs the shelter with street outreach and first-responder referral pathways.

**Eligibility Requirements**

For people experiencing homelessness who are Mesa-based; priority goes to Mesa's most vulnerable — families with young children, single women, seniors, veterans, domestic-violence survivors and people with disabilities. Admission is by referral only: referrals come through Mesa first responders (police, fire/medical, park rangers) and community/nonprofit partners; there is no walk-up or drop-in intake. Participants must follow program rules and stay engaged with case management.

**Population Served**

Mesa residents experiencing homelessness — especially families, single women, seniors (62+), veterans, people with disabilities and domestic-violence survivors. The program reports serving hundreds of children and seniors in the past year.

**How to Best Connect**

- Call the Mesa Homeless Resource Line: 480-644-HOPE (4673) — the city's public line for people experiencing homelessness in Mesa and for community members with questions or who want to refer or help. (City materials describe it as monitored on business days; call to confirm hours.)
- If you are a first responder or community partner: use the established referral pathways through the city / Office of Homeless Solutions.
- Do not send clients to the hotel — it is a closed campus with no walk-up services.
- Existing participants with case-status questions: Office of Homeless Solutions, 480-644-4273.

**Important Information to Know**

- Sunaire is not open as a shelter: the city renovated the former Sunaire Hotel at 6733 E. Main St. for this program, but on May 21, 2026 the City Council decided to keep Off the Streets at the Windermere Hotel instead; Sunaire may be sold. Do not send anyone to Sunaire.
- Operator change: Community Bridges, Inc. previously operated Off the Streets; in spring 2026 the city issued a notice of intent to award to Mercy House and reported Mercy House would manage day-to-day operations going forward — confirm the current operator and openings when you call.
- Capacity is tight: the city has reported waitlists (about a 6-week wait for some households, May 2026) and limited family shelter options in Mesa.
- Cost: no participant fee is published; the program is publicly funded.
- Mercy House is a nonprofit shelter operator (501(c)(3)) that also runs the 156-bed, city-owned Sue's Espacio shelter in Tempe at 2101 E. Apache Blvd., and other Arizona shelters.

Curated with corrected location/operator, the referral-only intake route via the Mesa Homeless Resource Line, and waitlist/transition cautions.

Mercy Housing (Mountain Plains region) also operates other affordable communities in the area, including Page Commons in Gilbert (55+) and Guadalupe Senior/Nuestro Pueblito in Guadalupe.
resources.hours: Office: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Affordable rental apartments for low-income seniors: 40 units at 333 E. 6th St., Mesa, with a community room, on-site laundry, health-and-wellness programming, and resident services (newsletters/calendars, activities and age-in-place programs). Applications are taken by Mercy Housing directly (online through the property page or at the office). Mercy Housing also lists other Arizona communities in the region: Page Commons in Gilbert (100 units, ages 55+, incomes 30–60% of area median) and Guadalupe Senior/Nuestro Pueblito in Guadalupe (22 units, seniors, incomes at or below 50% of area median).

**Eligibility Requirements**

Mesa Senior Meadows: low-income adults age 62 and older; income limits apply. Page Commons: ages 55+ with household incomes between 30% and 60% of the area median. Guadalupe Senior: low-income seniors with incomes at or below 50% of the area median. Mercy Housing screens applications for each property.

**Population Served**

Low-income older adults — age 62+ (Mesa Senior Meadows), 55+ (Page Commons), and low-income seniors (Guadalupe Senior).

**How to Best Connect**

- Call Mesa Senior Meadows at (480) 615-7893 (TTY 800-855-2880 or 711), Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; or apply via the “Apply Now” link on the property page at mercyhousing.org.
- Visit: 333 E. 6th Street, Mesa, AZ 85201 — about a five-minute walk from downtown Mesa.
- Other communities: Page Commons, 170 N. Oak St., Gilbert — (480) 813-4609; Guadalupe Senior/Nuestro Pueblito, 9403 S. Avenida Del Yaqui, Guadalupe — (480) 897-3273.

**Important Information to Know**

- Mesa Senior Meadows was listed as currently accepting applications in September 2026; availability and waitlists can change quickly — call before sending someone.
- Rent and subsidy terms are not published; ask about income limits, rent and whether project-based rental assistance applies.
- A third-party directory lists a separate property called “Mercy Housing Arizona I” at 520 N. Mesa Drive, Mesa (95 units); it does not appear on Mercy Housing's own site, so its owner/manager and waitlist status are unconfirmed — verify before relying on it, including any claimed link to City of Mesa Housing Authority waitlists.
- Applying to these properties is separate from City of Mesa Housing Authority public-housing/voucher waitlists; check the Housing Authority's current openings separately if a voucher is also needed.

resources.description: Native American Connections (NAC) is a Maricopa County coordinated entry point for Native American individuals experiencing homelessness and for youth (listed as ages 18–26), and it runs the HomeBase emergency youth shelters and drop-in centers in Phoenix and Surprise. Call 602-648-9739 to start a housing assessment for Native adults, or 602-263-5531 for youth/HomeBase; a longer-stay youth option (Saguaro Ki transitional housing) is reached through the same youth number.
resources.hours: Call to start intake; shelter and drop-in hours vary. NAC main office: 602-254-3247, Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Coordinated entry (housing assessment) for Native American individuals experiencing homelessness — NAC's Housing Specialist starts the assessment that connects to NAC's permanent supportive housing and shelter programs: 602-648-9739 or PSHinquiry@nativeconnections.org.
- Coordinated entry for youth (listed as ages 18–26) with services at the HomeBase locations: call 602-263-5531.
- HomeBase emergency youth shelters and drop-in centers — dormitory-style shelter, meals, computers, laundry, a small gym, counseling/behavioral-health support and case management at no cost. Sites: HomeBase Phoenix (24 beds) and HomeBase Surprise (40 dormitory-style beds); NAC describes 65 shelter beds across the two communities.
- Longer-stay youth housing: Saguaro Ki transitional living — 25 furnished studio apartments, six-month lease with rent at 30% of income, renewable up to 18 months.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Native adults: this coordinated entry point is specifically for Native American individuals experiencing homelessness — start with the Housing Specialist at 602-648-9739.
- Youth: must be experiencing homelessness; NAC's pages currently say 18–26 in some places and 18–24 or 18–25 in others, so confirm the age range when you call. You must provide ID verification and complete a housing assessment.
- Saguaro Ki adds income requirements (proof of income and about two months of work history at 25 hours/week).
- Single adults and youth only: NAC's access-point list notes these services are for single adults; families should call the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 or 211.

**Population Served**
- Native American individuals experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County (adult coordinated entry).
- Youth and young adults experiencing homelessness from all backgrounds — NAC says its services are open to all community members and reports 80% of its youth are BIPOC.
- Not a family shelter; families with children are routed to the Family Housing Hub.

**How to Best Connect**
- Native adults: call 602-648-9739 or email PSHinquiry@nativeconnections.org.
- Youth and HomeBase: call 602-263-5531 (also covers Saguaro Ki).
- Sites: HomeBase Phoenix, 931 E. Devonshire Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85014; HomeBase Surprise, 12215 W. Bell Rd, Surprise, AZ 85378. Drop-in and shelter hours vary — call before going.
- General NAC questions: 602-254-3247, Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.

**Important Information to Know**
- No cost is described for HomeBase shelter and drop-in services (NAC says 'at no cost'; community listings list no fees). Ask about any costs when you call; beds are limited and availability is not guaranteed.
- NAC's own pages disagree on the youth age cut-off (18–24, 18–25 and 18–26 all appear) — verify current eligibility before referral.
- Both intake numbers are current on NAC's website: 602-648-9739 for Native adult coordinated entry; 602-263-5531 for youth/HomeBase.
- NAC does not offer rental assistance. If NAC is not a fit: call 211; for families, Family Housing Hub 602-595-8700; for youth under 18, the county lists Safe Place (call or text 602-841-5799).
