Remaining limits: NAC's pages disagree on the youth age cut-off (18–24 vs 18–25 vs 18–26), and bed availability varies — call before sending anyone.

resources.description: New Life Center is one of Arizona's largest domestic-violence shelters — a 110-bed, trauma-informed emergency shelter in the Goodyear/West Valley area with a confidential location, serving singles and families from across Maricopa County, and one of the few that welcomes pets. Call 623-932-4404 to start shelter screening and to ask about survivor support services.
resources.hours: Shelter/support line: call 623-932-4404 — city and community listings describe it as a 24-hour line; call any time for screening. Business/office hours are not posted.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Emergency domestic-violence shelter: a 110-bed, trauma-informed shelter that meets basic needs and helps families move toward independent living — New Life Center reports 18,117 safe nights provided and 2,517 survivors served last year.
- Survivor support services: customized support plans for people impacted by domestic violence, sexual violence and human trafficking — advocacy and case management, trauma treatment, group and individual therapy, child care, and more — for shelter residents and for survivors living safely in the community.
- Sunshine Healing center: a stand-alone sexual-violence healing center open to anyone who has experienced sexual violence (including secondary victims); a police report is not required to receive services.
- Pet-friendly shelter: New Life Center is one of the few domestic-violence shelters in Arizona that welcomes pets, with onsite pet accommodations.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- For survivors of domestic violence, sexual violence or human trafficking; serves singles and families (ABC15's 2026 shelter list describes it as 'singles and families, pet friendly').
- New Life Center describes its shelter service as 'for shelter within Maricopa County.'
- Eligibility is determined by phone screening; the shelter has a confidential location, so there is no walk-in process.

**Population Served**
- Survivors and their children from across Maricopa County — New Life Center reports serving more than 1,000 children and adults each year.
- Community directories list served populations including women, men, teens and families; call to discuss your household's situation.
- Pet owners — one of the only pet-welcoming domestic-violence shelters in Arizona.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call 623-932-4404: New Life Center directs people seeking shelter or support services to this number, and city/community listings describe it as a 24-hour line, so you can call at any time for screening.
- Email info@newlifectr.org is for general agency questions only — not for shelter requests.
- The shelter is in the Goodyear/West Valley area with a confidential address; do not go to the location without screening. Ask about access from Mesa, transportation help and current bed availability.
- Mailing address: PO Box 5005, Goodyear, AZ 85338. Spanish-language pages are available on the website; ask for a Spanish-speaking advocate if needed.

**Important Information to Know**
- In 2026 the countywide SafeDVS referral hotline ended full service and now directs callers to local shelter services (ABC15 reported the change to a recorded message on May 15, 2026). Some county pages still list a SAFEDVS crisis line (480-890-3039) — calling New Life Center directly is the practical route.
- Bed availability varies; calling does not guarantee a bed. No fees are published — ask about any costs during screening.
- Because the shelter is West Valley-based and its location is confidential, ask how Mesa-area survivors are served and what transportation options exist.
- Safety tip: call from a safe phone; the website includes an emergency-exit button for people using a shared device.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Listed as a Maricopa County coordinated entry access point for single adults experiencing homelessness — a walk-in housing assessment and referral into Coordinated Entry shelter and housing programs (per NAC's current access-point list and other provider guides).
- CASS has described the Norton & Ramsey Social Justice Empowerment Center as its West Valley navigation hub for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness, with housing support, case management and partner services (2023 CASS materials; not reconfirmed as current).

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Single adults experiencing homelessness (adults 18+). Families with children are routed to the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 or 211.
- Confirm by phone that walk-in assessments are currently offered before traveling.

**Population Served**
- Adults experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness in Glendale and the West Valley, per City of Glendale materials; part of the countywide system for single adults.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call 623-207-8902 first. Address: 7031 N 56th Ave, Glendale, AZ 85301. Reported hours: Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m. (a city list shows 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; some CoC materials describe the number as a 24/7 resource hotline).
- If the center is unreachable or no longer operating: use the county's central single-adult entry point — Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S 12th Ave, Phoenix, AZ 85007; 602-229-5155 — or call 211 for the nearest coordinated entry point.

**Important Information to Know**
- Unresolved: whether NREC is still an active walk-in coordinated entry access point. Several current listings (including NAC's access-point list and provider guides) still show it at 7031 N 56th Ave with phone 623-207-8902 and weekday hours, but CASS's own current website no longer mentions the Glendale center and directs single adults to call the Welcome Center at 602-229-5155 for intake, and the City of Glendale's current homeless-services page lists the Brian Garcia Welcome Center for individual assessments.
- Do not make a trip without confirming by phone first.
- Families with children cannot use this single-adult entry point — call the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 or 211.

resources.address: Oxford House, Inc. national office: 1010 Wayne Avenue, Suite 300, Silver Spring, MD 20910 (houses are located in communities nationwide, including Arizona)
resources.description: Oxford House is a national network of self-run, self-supported sober-living homes for adults recovering from substance use disorder, with houses in Arizona including the Phoenix metro/Mesa area. There is no time limit on staying; residents share expenses (about $125–$250 a week per Oxford House's FAQ), and rooms are filled by a vote of current residents after an interview. Use the official vacancy locator at oxfordvacancies.com or call (800) 689-6411.
resources.hours: No fixed hours; call a house contact to arrange an interview (interview times vary by house and are listed on the vacancy locator).
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Sober-living recovery residences: shared houses run democratically by the residents, providing a drug- and alcohol-free living environment with peer support; no paid clinical staff and no fixed length of stay (average stay is about a year, and some members stay longer).
- Application pathway: find houses with openings on the official vacancy locator (oxfordvacancies.com), call the house contact to arrange an interview, or use the online application to send your information to all nearby houses with openings; current residents vote on acceptance.
- Oxford House World Services can answer questions and help with referrals: (800) 689-6411 or (301) 587-2916.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Adults in recovery from drug and alcohol addiction (substance use disorder) who commit to staying drug- and alcohol-free; anyone who returns to using alcohol or drugs is immediately expelled.
- No specific amount of sober/clean time is required; Oxford House says people generally come into a house after a 28-day rehabilitation program or at least a 5–10-day detoxification program.
- You must be able to pay your equal share of house expenses and live without being disruptive; acceptance is by a vote of the current residents after an interview.
- Houses are gender-specific (men's houses, women's houses, and some houses for parents with children).

**Population Served**
- Adults in recovery from substance use disorder, including people leaving treatment or detox and people rebuilding income and stability; the network includes houses across the U.S., with Arizona houses in the Phoenix metro area including Mesa.

**How to Best Connect**
- Official vacancy locator: oxfordvacancies.com — filter by state/county to see houses with openings, each listing a contact person and an interview time; phone before visiting (there is no walk-in admission).
- Online application: the 'Apply Online' option at oxfordvacancies.com sends your application to all houses near you with openings.
- Phone: Oxford House, Inc. at (800) 689-6411 (toll-free) or (301) 587-2916; national office: 1010 Wayne Avenue, Suite 300, Silver Spring, MD 20910.
- For Mesa/Phoenix metro houses, search Arizona in the locator and follow up with each house contact. Arizona has no separate state website — use these national routes.

**Important Information to Know**
- Cost: each member pays an 'equal expense share' (EES) covering rent, utilities and household staples; Oxford House's FAQ says the amount varies from house to house and can range from about $125 to $250 per week — ask each house. Move-in usually requires a nonrefundable fee plus payment for the first two weeks.
- Vacancies and house lists change often — check the live locator rather than relying on a saved list; if one house does not accept you, apply at another.
- Oxford Houses are not treatment programs and have no clinical staff; they are self-run. Staying requires sobriety, paying your share and not being disruptive.
- The network is large nationally (more than 3,500 houses) — plan to contact more than one house and ask each about their interview time.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A community navigation office (Mesa coordinated-entry access point) at the Paz de Cristo community center. Staff help people who are homeless or unstably housed get connected to housing and shelter resources, including shelter lists, low-income housing information and the coordinated-entry assessment process, plus behavioral health referrals (COPA Health), employment search help, Arizona ID and birth-certificate assistance, and AHCCCS and SNAP applications. The same center runs a daily evening meal (about 5:15–6:30 p.m.), showers (schedule varies by season), clothing, periodic food boxes and a mail service, so people who come for a meal can also ask about the navigation office.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No eligibility rules are published specifically for the navigation office; coordinated entry serves people who are homeless or need housing help in Maricopa County. Call first to confirm requirements and whether an appointment is needed. For the center's own services: the evening meal is open to anyone in need; photo ID is required for food boxes and mail service, and food boxes also require proof of local residence within the last 30 days.

**Population Served**
People who are homeless or housing-insecure in Mesa and nearby East Valley communities. Paz de Cristo serves adults, seniors, families and children (children must be accompanied by an adult), and its services are available in English and Spanish.

**How to Best Connect**
Visit 424 W. Broadway Rd., Mesa, AZ 85210. Posted hours for the navigation office are Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–3 p.m.; call before going to confirm the office is staffed that day. Phone options: 480-993-7740 or 480-620-8695 (COPA Health community navigation office) and 480-464-2370 (Paz de Cristo main line). COPA Health's main office: 480-969-3800, 924 N. Country Club Dr., Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
This is an assessment and connection point, not an emergency shelter — visiting or calling does not guarantee a shelter bed or housing; it starts the connection and assessment process. No cost information is published for the navigation services; ask when you call. Hours and staffing should be confirmed by phone before sending someone. The office is located inside a community center that serves meals, which makes it reachable for people who are unsheltered.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A free residential recovery program for people who are homeless and/or struggling with addiction. It provides safe housing (160 beds for young men and 45 beds for young women), structured daily programming, addiction-recovery classes, counseling and mentoring, an onsite medical center, a behavioral health team, eye care and dental care, physical wellness programs, life-skills training and career/job preparation. The center reports serving about 500 people a year through this program. The organization also runs a crisis-response outreach team and a separate residential program for survivors of human trafficking (Where Hope Lives).

**Eligibility Requirements**
The program is for men and women dealing with addiction and homelessness; all services are described as completely free, and the center says its services are not conditional on a person's faith. Specific rules — age range, medical or mental-health criteria, program length — are not published. Call the men's or women's intake line to confirm fit and requirements.

**Population Served**
Men and women; the center describes its beds as for young men and young women and serves people leaving homelessness, addiction and related crises. Exact age limits are not published — confirm by phone. The organization also describes serving people who have experienced incarceration or foster care (and a separate program serves trafficking survivors).

**How to Best Connect**
Call the program directly: men's Life Recovery 602-816-6582; women's Life Recovery 602-706-1876; general assistance 602-346-8716; main line 602-346-8700. Or use the contact form on the Get Help page: phoenixdreamcenter.org/get-help. The page advises that call lines are busy and asks callers to allow up to 72 business hours for a response; if you are in an emergency or an unsafe situation, call 911 or seek medical care. Location: 3210 Grand Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85017 (public tours Tuesdays at noon; for help, call first).

**Important Information to Know**
There is no charge for the recovery program or its services. The program is faith-based (Christ-centered) while the center states services are not conditional on faith. Current openings and wait times are not published — ask when you call. Length of stay, age limits and screening rules are not published and older community listings may not reflect current policy, so verify before referring.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Residential recovery for women and their children at the Changing Lives Center for Women & Children. The core program, Transformations, is a 12-month faith-based residency with four 13-week phases: addiction and mental-health treatment classes, individual and group counseling, case management, life skills, workforce development and job preparation, legal support, medical care and medication access, and transportation to appointments. Childcare is provided for infants and toddlers, and a local elementary-school partnership keeps school-age children in class; parent reunification is a goal when child-welfare involvement exists. Graduates receive six months of aftercare plus alumni support. The first step can be short-term residential care (Rescue-Assess-Place): a typical 7–30 day stay with food, a bed, clothing, showers, assessment and referrals.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For women dealing with homelessness, addiction and/or trauma; mothers may bring their children. The programs are voluntary — the person must want change. Intake includes an assessment to place each person in the right program; age and medical criteria are not published. No fee is stated for the short-term program, and basic needs are covered in the year-long program — confirm any other costs at intake.

**Population Served**
Women, including mothers with children, experiencing homelessness, addiction and trauma. The Mission's short-term care also serves women fleeing domestic violence. Men are served separately at the Transforming Lives Center (1801 S. 35th Ave., Phoenix).

**How to Best Connect**
Call (602) 233-3000 to schedule an intake appointment. Intake office hours: Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; appointments are required and walk-ins are not allowed, but same-day appointments are often available. Location: Changing Lives Center for Women & Children, 338 N. 15th Ave., Phoenix, AZ 85007. Family members may call on behalf of a willing loved one. Program information: phoenixrescuemission.org/help/substance-abuse-trauma/recovery-program/.

**Important Information to Know**
The program is faith-based (Christ-centered). The short-term stay is typically 7–30 days; the recovery program runs 12 months in four 13-week phases. Appointments are required — no walk-ins. Current capacity, wait times and exact screening rules are not published; call to ask about openings. Some older listings show different intake numbers; (602) 233-3000 is the current intake line.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A hotline to request help from the Mission's street-outreach team: Hope Coach vehicles travel the streets of Maricopa County with water, hygiene kits (Hope Totes), seasonal items and case management from peer-support-certified case managers, help obtaining IDs and documents, and connection to housing or recovery programs. Through the Housing Assistance Program, staff help with housing applications, documents, locating an apartment, vouchers (decided case-by-case), security deposits and basic move-in needs, furniture and household items, and continuing case management. The Mission's short-term residential care (7–30 days) and recovery programs also start through the same intake line.

**Eligibility Requirements**
No eligibility rules are published for the outreach hotline; it serves people experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. Residential programs have their own screening and are voluntary; housing vouchers are generally state- or federally funded and decided case-by-case. Requirements differ by program — ask when you call. Families with children are generally routed to Maricopa County's Family Housing Hub (602-595-8700).

**Population Served**
People living unsheltered in Maricopa County; the Mission describes outreach to men, women and children on the streets, and its case managers place hundreds of people into housing or recovery programs each year. Spanish-language pages and materials are available; ask about Spanish-speaking staff when you call.

**How to Best Connect**
Call the street-outreach hotline at 602-346-3361 for Hope Coach visit requests. If it does not connect, use the main line 602-233-3000, which current pages also list for outreach visits, intake and housing help. Give your nearest cross streets when requesting a visit. Online: help/inquiry form at phoenixrescuemission.org/help. Email: outreach@phxmission.org. Address for mail/administration: Mission Support Center, 1540 W. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85007 — call first; services are mobile or by appointment. Residential campuses: men's, 1801 S. 35th Ave.; women and children's, 338 N. 15th Ave.

**Important Information to Know**
This is not a walk-in emergency shelter — help starts with a phone call, and outreach teams come to people on the street. For emergencies, call 911. No fees are listed for Mission programs; the short-term program states no fee and housing vouchers are case-by-case. Hotline hours and outreach schedules are not published — call to confirm; teams serve Maricopa County. Phoenix Rescue Mission serves as a Maricopa County coordinated-entry point for adults without children through this outreach hotline. Capacity and wait times are not published.

resources.description: Immediate crisis help for youth ages 12–17 in Maricopa County who are homeless, have run away, or need help for any reason. Youth can call or text for help, or walk into any designated Safe Place site — all QuikTrip stores and Valley Metro locations plus libraries, fire departments, transit stops and participating businesses — ask staff for Safe Place, and wait in a safe, private area until responders arrive to arrange placement and services.
resources.hours: Crisis line answered 24 hours a day; Safe Place sites (all QuikTrip and Valley Metro locations, plus libraries, fire departments, transit stops and participating businesses) can be used during each site's public hours. resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Safe Place is a national youth-outreach program. Youth ages 12–17 who have run away, are homeless, or need help for any reason can use it to get immediate assistance. A youth can go into any participating Safe Place site — look for the Safe Place sign — ask for help, and wait in a safe, private area until trained staff arrive. All QuikTrip stores and Valley Metro locations in Maricopa County are designated Safe Place sites; libraries, fire departments, public transit stops, and other participating businesses also display the sign. Youth (or anyone helping them) can also call the 24-hour crisis line at 602-841-5799 or text SAFE and their location or address to 44357. The local Safe Place agency responds and can arrange a safe placement; Child Crisis Arizona, the local agency, has said it reserves beds in its youth Independent Living Program for youth who need an overnight place to stay.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Youth ages 12–17 in Maricopa County who are runaway, homeless, or 'seeking assistance for any reason,' including family conflict and abuse. No income test, application, or formal referral is described — help starts by calling, texting, or going to a Safe Place site. The program serves youth only; adults need different entry points in the county's homeless services system.

**Population Served**
Youth ages 12–17 across Maricopa County, including Mesa and the East Valley, through valley-wide sites and transit access. Users include youth who are homeless, have run away, or are in an unsafe or unstable family situation.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call the 24-hour crisis line: 602-841-5799.
- Text SAFE plus your current location or address to 44357 (4HELP).
- Or go to any Safe Place site and ask staff for help: all QuikTrip and Valley Metro locations, plus listed sites at libraries, fire departments, transit stops and participating local businesses. Staff will contact the Safe Place line, and the youth can wait on site until help arrives; site staff can make the contact for a youth who arrives in person.
Use the current instructions above (see the note below about an older text number).

**Important Information to Know**
- The currently published instruction is to text SAFE and your location to 44357; an older number (69866) appears in earlier guides and was used to locate the nearest site. Use 44357 or the crisis line to avoid confusion.
- Child Crisis Arizona has been the local home of Safe Place since 2021 (the program was previously operated by Tumbleweed Center for Youth Development); the county's current help page still lists the same crisis line for youth ages 12–17.
- What happens after contact depends on the situation and bed availability; overnight shelter is not guaranteed, and no costs or fees are published — ask when calling.

resources.description: Residential behavioral-health treatment with integrated substance-use care and built-in supportive housing at licensed recovery homes in the Phoenix–Scottsdale area. The core model is a recommended 90-day residential program, with step-down to PHP, IOP, virtual IOP, sober living, and case management; North Phoenix sites include SRC 28th (17632 N 28th St) and SRC Friess (4324 E Friess Dr). Entry is through admissions and a clinical assessment, not a rental application.
resources.hours: Intake hours are not published — call to schedule a screening. The residential program is a live-in, 24-hour living environment.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Residential (inpatient-style) behavioral-health treatment with integrated substance-use care; a 90-day residential stay is the recommended core program, with stabilization and, when clinically appropriate, detox support as part of the plan.
- Supportive housing is built into the residential program — clients live in agency-operated recovery homes during treatment — and continued care includes sober living, a partial hospitalization program (PHP), intensive outpatient (IOP), virtual IOP, case management, medication management (including medication-assisted treatment for opioid use), and individual, group, and family therapy.
- Multiple Phoenix-area locations. Public records list SRC 28th (17632 N 28th St), SRC Friess / Sanctuary Sober Living (4324 E Friess Dr), and additional sites such as Rose Garden (2027 E Rose Garden Ln), Cave Creek, and Desert Cove; the administrative address is 11645 N Cave Creek Rd, Phoenix 85020.
- Discharge planning covers next-step housing, employment readiness, and ongoing recovery support.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Adults who need residential-level care for substance use and/or co-occurring mental-health conditions; admission follows a clinical assessment arranged through the admissions/intake line.
- A public provider listing describes the Friess residence as serving adult men ages 18–25 and 26–64, and the agency describes a male 'brotherhood' community — confirm current gender and age rules for the specific site at intake.
- The agency also runs a separate adolescent program (ages 12–17) at its Roadrunner Home in Phoenix; that is a different program from the adult recovery residences described here.
- No income-based eligibility is published; payment and coverage are reviewed at intake.

**Population Served**
Adults (18+) in the Phoenix metro area with substance-use and co-occurring mental-health needs who require residential structure and recovery housing; at least one residence serves adult men. Separate adolescent services exist for ages 12–17.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call admissions at 877-978-8783, intake at 480-309-9945, or the main line at 602-612-3816.
- Website: sanctuaryrecoverycenters.com (contact form and insurance verification). Ask directly about current openings, an assessment appointment, which residence fits (SRC 28th vs. Friess), and coverage.
- Addresses to reference: 17632 N 28th St, Phoenix, AZ 85032; 4324 E Friess Dr, Phoenix, AZ 85032.
- If you have AHCCCS/Medicaid or private insurance, ask intake to confirm network participation for the specific site before committing.

**Important Information to Know**
- This is treatment-linked housing: entry is through a clinical admissions process (assessment), not a housing waitlist; expect a structured program rather than a standard lease.
- Costs are not published, and coverage signals conflict: SAMHSA's national directory and an Arizona Medicaid plan directory list the agency and its sites, while one third-party listing says private insurance only with no sliding fee scale. Verify cost and coverage for the specific residence at intake; low- or no-cost placement is not established.
- Bed availability and exact referral requirements are not published; call for current capacity. The company is registered in the national provider registry as a substance-abuse rehabilitation facility and describes its homes as licensed behavioral health residential properties.
- Phone numbers differ across directories (602-612-3816, 602-675-2330, 480-309-9945); admissions staff can route you to the right line.

resources.hours: Office: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed Saturday and Sunday.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Permanent affordable rental housing through more than 170 scattered single-family homes under ARM of Save the Family.
- Co-developed affordable communities: Escobedo at Verde Vista in Mesa (families and individuals, with a focus on people facing behavioral and mental-health challenges); Valor on 8th in Tempe (veteran-focused); and Phoenix Scholar House (in development).
- Each community includes a Save the Family Resource Center where a case manager provides workforce-development workshops and connections to community resources; Save the Family's supportive services — career help, budgeting, parenting and life-skills classes, and mental-health support — are available to families living in ARM housing.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Low-income households; ARM is described as permanent low-income housing.
- Individual communities may have their own focus (for example, Escobedo at Verde Vista serves families and individuals, including people with behavioral and mental-health challenges).
- Income limits, rental application procedures, and waitlists are not published — call Save the Family to ask how to apply or get on a list.

**Population Served**
Low-income individuals and families in Maricopa County, with a Mesa/East Valley presence (Mesa office and Escobedo at Verde Vista). Some housing is targeted to specific groups (people with behavioral and mental-health challenges; veterans at Valor on 8th).

**How to Best Connect**
- Call (480) 898-0228 Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m., and ask specifically about 'ARM of Save the Family' rentals, availability, and how to apply.
- Online: savethefamily.org → 'How We Help' → 'ARM of Save the Family' for program information. Office: 125 E. University Dr., Mesa, AZ 85201.
- If your family is currently experiencing homelessness and you are seeking Save the Family's supportive housing programs, the county's family entry point is the Family Housing Hub, 3307 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, 602-595-8700 — ask there about Save the Family programs. ARM is the organization's affordable-housing side, separate from its temporary and rapid-rehousing programs.

**Important Information to Know**
- ARM is permanent affordable housing, not emergency shelter or short-term rental assistance; residents pay rent (rent amounts and income limits are not published — ask).
- Vacancies and waitlist status are not published; call to confirm current availability.
- A.R.M. stands for Affordable Rental Movement; current materials present it as 'ARM of Save the Family.' Save the Family's 2025 annual report and current website describe ARM as its affordable-housing program with 170+ homes, so the program is current; individual unit availability and the application route still need to be confirmed directly with the office.

resources.description: Rapid Rehousing for families with children facing homelessness in Mesa and Maricopa County — help finding housing plus time-limited, stepped-down rental assistance — paired with Save the Family's FACES (Families Adult and Children Empowerment Services) supportive services, case management, and children's programming on the path to permanent housing and self-sufficiency.
resources.hours: Office: Monday–Friday 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed weekends. Family intake goes through the Family Housing Hub — call 602-595-8700 for current intake hours.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Rapid Rehousing: help locating housing in the community (families can sign their own leases) and time-limited, stepped-down rental assistance, described as including help with deposits and application fees and rent support that decreases as the family's income grows.
- Case management: a case manager helps parents set and reach goals — employment, budgeting, benefits, documentation, referrals — throughout the family's journey and after move-in.
- FACES (Families Adult and Children Empowerment Services): supportive services aimed at helping clients achieve permanent housing, income, and self-sufficiency, including parenting and life-skills education, mental-health support, and programs for children and youth.
- Additional supports: career services, budgeting and parenting classes, in-house mental-health support, and children's services such as school supplies, counseling, and activities.
- Save the Family also operates Tenant-Based Rental Assistance and Step Up to Independence transitional housing; ask which programs are accepting families now.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Families with children who are experiencing homelessness; the program serves parents and children together, and children's programming is a standard part of services.
- Families in Maricopa County are screened through the Family Housing Hub, the county's coordinated-entry point for families — call 602-595-8700 before or alongside contacting Save the Family.
- Specific income rules and required documents are not published; intake staff will explain what is needed.

**Population Served**
Families with children who are homeless or facing homelessness in Mesa, the East Valley, and Maricopa County. Program descriptions include families in shelter and families who are doubled up, living in cars, or couch-surfing.

**How to Best Connect**
- First step for families: call the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 (3307 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ) — the county's coordinated entry for families — and ask about Save the Family's programs.
- Direct questions: Save the Family, (480) 898-0228, 125 E. University Dr., Mesa, AZ 85201; office hours Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Ask for Rapid Rehousing and FACES program information.
- Website: savethefamily.org (see 'How We Help') for current program descriptions.

**Important Information to Know**
- Rapid Rehousing is time-limited, stepped-down rental assistance — not a guaranteed long-term subsidy or an immediate placement. Current openings depend on funding and capacity, which are not published; call to check.
- Eligibility is not guaranteed by the office; families are screened through the coordinated-entry process, and participation includes working with a case manager.
- Save the Family describes support continuing about 6–12 months as families build income and stability, with follow-up after exit.
- Costs: families take on more of the rent as assistance steps down; exact rent-share and any fees are not published — ask intake.

resources.description: St. Vincent de Paul's Phoenix campus is a central charitable-help location in Maricopa County and is listed as a coordinated entry access point for seniors experiencing homelessness. It connects people to shelter and housing resources and offers one-time rent/utility help through neighborhood church conferences, food and meals, weather relief, and medical/dental services. Call 602-266-4673 (602-266-HOPE) to confirm what is available before going.
resources.hours: Main campus page lists Monday–Saturday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; a senior coordinated-entry listing shows Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–4 p.m.; call before visiting.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Coordinates access to shelter, services and housing resources as a listed coordinated entry access point for seniors experiencing homelessness at the 420 W. Watkins Rd. campus.
- One-time rent, mortgage and utility assistance through volunteer-run St. Vincent de Paul conferences based in neighborhood Catholic churches (each conference is limited to its own area).
- Food boxes and hot meals; shelter and seasonal weather relief; medical and dental clinics for people without insurance; and pet services for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness.
- Help finding the correct neighborhood conference for your address.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Call for eligibility screening; required documents depend on the service, and fees vary by service.
- Rent/utility assistance is one-time and restricted to the neighborhood served by each volunteer conference.
- Medical clinic: uninsured or under-insured patients. Dental clinic: uninsured patients (adult dental uses a lottery).
- Coordinated entry assistance is intended for people experiencing homelessness; the published entry-point listing focuses on seniors.

**Population Served**
- People in Maricopa County who are experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness; the coordinated-entry listing specifically names seniors experiencing homelessness.
- SVdP's wider programs serve individuals and families, including older adults, veterans and adults with disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call 602-266-4673 (602-266-HOPE); email info@svdpaz.org. Campus: 420 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003.
- Hours vary by listing: the campus page shows Monday–Saturday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; the senior coordinated-entry listing shows Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–4 p.m. Call before visiting.
- For rent/utility help, find your neighborhood conference at stvincentdepaul.net (Get Help) or call 2-1-1; if no conference serves your area, call 602-619-9903.
- Shelter and transitional-housing questions are handled on a separate line: 602-850-6900, 8 a.m.–3 p.m.

**Important Information to Know**
- Coordinated entry routing differs by population: Maricopa County's current homeless-services page directs single adults (Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 602-229-5155), families (Family Housing Hub, 602-595-8700), veterans (VA Community Resource and Referral Center, 602-248-6040), youth (Safe Place) and domestic-violence survivors (SAFEDVS, 480-890-3039) to other entry points, and SVdP is not on that list. Confirm which entry point fits before going specifically for coordinated entry.
- Help is limited and not guaranteed: conference funds, hours and capacity vary, some services are by appointment or lottery, and no place is reserved by calling.

Two open points are preserved rather than hidden: campus hours differ across listings (8–4 vs 8–5), and the county's current entry-point page routes most populations elsewhere. The phone route 602-266-4673 remains a responsible referral path, so no needs-resolution barrier.

resources.description: Ozanam Manor is a St. Vincent de Paul interim/transitional housing community in Phoenix for men and women experiencing homelessness who are 55 or older or 18+ with a disability, with select beds for veterans. Residents get a bed in a dorm-style community, case management, activities and help moving into permanent housing. Intake starts with a phone screening at 602-850-6900 (8 a.m.–3 p.m.), followed by an in-person interview. No cost if you have no income; otherwise 30% of income.
resources.hours: Intake/screening calls: 8 a.m.–3 p.m. (602-850-6900).
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- Interim/transitional housing at Ozanam Manor, part of St. Vincent de Paul's Interim Housing Communities in Phoenix.
- Residents have a bed in a dorm-style community and can join group activities and life-skills courses; case managers meet one-on-one to help with paperwork and work toward independent living and permanent housing.
- The same intake line also screens for SVdP's other transitional sites — De Paul Manor and Rosalie's Place (310–320 W. Watkins Rd.).

**Eligibility Requirements**
- Adults 55+; adults 18+ living with a disability; select beds for veterans at Ozanam Manor (veterans are asked to enter through the VA).
- SVdP's transitional housing intake also lists adults 18+ who are working or looking for work (its workforce housing); ask which site fits.
- A phone pre-screen is followed by a face-to-face interview with a case manager to confirm the program is a good fit.

**Population Served**
- Men and women experiencing homelessness who are older adults (55+) or adults 18+ with a physical or mental disability; veterans (select beds).
- SVdP describes its interim housing communities as serving veterans, seniors and adults living with disabilities.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call 602-850-6900 between 8 a.m. and 3 p.m. for eligibility screening; then an in-person interview if screened in.
- Location: 320 W. Watkins Rd., Phoenix, AZ 85003. Program page: stvincentdepaul.net/locations/ozanam-manor.
- Veterans: work through the VA to enter Ozanam Manor's veteran beds.

**Important Information to Know**
- Cost: no cost if you have no income; otherwise 30% of income.
- Bed availability and waitlists vary; a pre-screen does not guarantee a bed.
- Age rule: current SVdP materials say 55+; older listings sometimes said 50+ — confirm at screening.
- Ozanam Manor is separate from SVdP's coordinated-entry/charity campus nearby; transitional housing intake runs on its own phone line (602-850-6900).

resources.description: Sojourner Center runs one of Maricopa County's largest domestic-violence shelters and a 24/7 hotline. It offers up to 120 days of emergency shelter with 24-hour staff, children's services and pet support, plus transitional housing for up to two years. Call the 24/7 hotline at (602) 244-0089 for safety planning, screening and current availability; the shelter location is confidential.
resources.hours: 24/7 hotline; main office phone during business hours (hours not published); shelter location is confidential and access is by phone.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- 24/7 hotline for crisis support, safety planning and direct access to shelter when available.
- Emergency shelter: up to 120 days of services in a secure living area with 24-hour staff support; trauma-informed case management; three meals daily; children's and youth services; a licensed Quality First child development center (birth to age 12); pet companion services (pet daycare and support); support groups and workshops; on-site community partner services (health, behavioral health, housing, workforce); and lay legal support for orders of protection and court.
- Transitional housing: up to two years of supportive services in 32 apartments; referrals by email at TransitionalHousingReferrals@sojournercenter.org.
- Community outreach: mobile case management and safety planning for survivors who are not seeking shelter; reachable at (602) 244-0089 during business hours.
- Sojourner says it operates about 30% of Maricopa County's emergency shelter beds for domestic-violence survivors and their children.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- For people affected by domestic violence, sexual assault or human trafficking, including adults and children; call the hotline for screening and current availability.
- Emergency shelter stays up to 120 days; transitional housing up to 2 years by referral.
- Pets are supported; confirm pet logistics at screening.

**Population Served**
- Survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault and human trafficking in the Phoenix area (Maricopa County), including adults and children; families with children are served.

**How to Best Connect**
- Call the 24-hour hotline at (602) 244-0089 — call 911 if in immediate danger. The hotline does screening and can connect directly to shelter when available.
- Main office: (602) 244-0997; info@sojournercenter.org; mail: P.O. Box 20156, Phoenix, AZ 85036. The shelter location is confidential and access is by phone.
- Transitional housing referrals: TransitionalHousingReferrals@sojournercenter.org.
- Other support: National Domestic Violence Hotline 800-799-7233; 2-1-1 Arizona.

**Important Information to Know**
- Availability varies and waitlists are possible. Maricopa County's current homeless-services page lists SAFEDVS (480-890-3039 or 844-723-3387) as the county domestic-violence crisis line; Sojourner's own 24/7 hotline remains active, and Sojourner says it strengthened hotline capacity during the county centralized-line transition.
- Name check: some older lists tie "Autumn House" to this shelter; current public information describes Autumn House as a separate East Valley shelter run by A New Leaf (480-890-3039). If you were told to call "Autumn House," confirm the agency.
- No fee is published for shelter; confirm program rules, pet arrangements and child development center enrollment when you call.

resources.resolutionReason: Usable: official pages confirm the 24/7 hotline, up-to-120-day emergency shelter, two-year transitional housing, children's and pet services, and continued direct 24/7 screening after the county centralized-line transition. The "Autumn House" element of the original name is not supported for Sojourner (Autumn House is a separate A New Leaf East Valley shelter), so it is flagged for accuracy rather than repeated; availability varies but the hotline is a responsible referral route.

resources.description: Southwest Behavioral & Health Services (SB&H) is a long-time HOPWA housing provider for people living with HIV/AIDS in Maricopa and Pinal counties. Its HOPWA program provides transitional housing (up to 24 months) with case management and help moving toward permanent housing, and referrals also come through Care Directions' Housing Information Services. Call SB&H at 602-285-4288 or 602-265-8338 to ask about current openings.
resources.hours: No walk-in hours published; call SB&H or Care Directions during business hours. City of Phoenix HOPWA Central Intake: Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
- HOPWA transitional housing: leased or agency-owned units for up to 24 months with intensive supportive services, aimed at moving residents into permanent housing; residents contribute a portion of income toward rent.
- Housing case management and support: intake, screening and assessment; individualized housing plans; unit oversight; referrals and follow-up; help with health, income and community resources.
- SB&H is a long-time HOPWA provider in the Phoenix area and describes itself as the largest provider of housing and support services for persons with HIV (HOPWA).
- The broader City of Phoenix HOPWA network (accessed through the routes below) also offers permanent supportive housing, permanent independent housing, tenant-based rental assistance through the Section 8 office, short-term rent/mortgage/utility assistance (STRMU), move-in assistance (PHP), housing information/referrals and housing advocacy.

**Eligibility Requirements**
- At least one household member diagnosed with HIV or AIDS; household income at or below 80% of the Area Median Income; currently living in Maricopa or Pinal counties.
- STRMU requires that the household is not receiving housing or utility assistance from another housing program.
- Transitional housing residents pay part of their income toward rent; ask about documentation (HIV diagnosis, income) at intake.

**Population Served**
- Low-income people living with HIV/AIDS and their families in Maricopa and Pinal counties (Phoenix metro and Pinal County).

**How to Best Connect**
- Call SB&H: 602-285-4288 (general intake/appointment help) or 602-265-8338 (main office); website sbhservices.org (Services → Housing). Ask for the HOPWA housing program.
- Referral route: Care Directions Housing Information Services, 602-264-2273 — the City's HOPWA housing information program, which matches callers to HOPWA housing providers in Maricopa and Pinal counties (1366 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85014).
- For STRMU/move-in assistance: City of Phoenix Human Services Central Intake, (602) 534-AIDE (2433), choose option #3; or apply online at phoenix.gov/HOPWA; business hours Monday–Friday 8 a.m.–5 p.m.
- SB&H's HOPWA housing staff work weekdays; call ahead to confirm hours.

**Important Information to Know**
- Phone numbers have changed over time: older City/county materials list SB&H HOPWA contacts at 602-318-1715 and 480-589-5890 — these may be program-specific or dated. Start with SB&H 602-285-4288 / 602-265-8338 and Care Directions 602-264-2273.
- Availability and waitlists vary; HOPWA eligibility is income- and diagnosis-based; this is not an emergency shelter — if you need shelter tonight, call 2-1-1.
- Help is limited to Maricopa and Pinal counties.
- Costs: transitional housing has an income-based resident contribution; STRMU/move-in help depends on eligibility and available funding.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Prisma Community Care — formerly Southwest Center for HIV/AIDS — is a Phoenix HIV/AIDS health and wellness organization that people living with HIV/AIDS can contact about housing assistance. It is one of the local organizations funded through the City of Phoenix HOPWA (Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS) program. HOPWA housing help in this area includes short-term rent, mortgage and utility payments to stop an eviction, foreclosure or utility shut-off; move-in costs such as security deposits, first and last month's rent, and application fees; and housing case management. Ask specifically about HOPWA housing assistance when you call.

**Eligibility Requirements**
At least one household member must be diagnosed with HIV or AIDS; household income must be at or below 80% of area median income; the household must currently live in Maricopa or Pinal County; and for short-term rent/utility help, the household generally must not already be receiving housing or utility assistance from another housing program. Prisma serves people living with HIV and the wider community; final eligibility for each housing program is decided by the agency administering it.

**Population Served**
People living with or affected by HIV/AIDS and their families, including partners and spouses. The organization also serves 2SLGBTQIA+ people, people of color, and uninsured or underinsured Arizonans. Services are provided in English and Spanish, with interpretation available for other languages.

**How to Best Connect**
Call Prisma at 602-307-5330 (1101 N. Central Ave., Ste. 200, Phoenix; email contactus@prismacare.org) and ask about HOPWA housing assistance. The citywide HOPWA intake is also available: call 602-534-AIDE (602-534-2433), choose option 3, then choose a Family Services Center, then option 3 again to speak with staff — say you are asking about HOPWA. You can also apply online at phoenix.gov/HOPWA. Intake hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. The office is in downtown Phoenix; plan for a drive or transit trip from Mesa.

**Important Information to Know**
The organization changed its name from Southwest Center for HIV/AIDS on January 1, 2025 — both names mean the same place. Prisma's website highlights medical and wellness services and does not spell out its housing help, so confirm what housing support is currently available for your situation when you call; the citywide HOPWA intake line is the most reliable route to HOPWA housing programs. HOPWA help is grant-funded for eligible households and is not guaranteed — waitlists, appointment availability and funding vary. Published office hours differ slightly between Prisma's website and other directories, so call before visiting. Expect to verify HIV diagnosis, income and county of residence during eligibility screening.

resources.description: Rotating overnight emergency shelter for adults experiencing homelessness (men and women), run by Tempe Community Action Agency with faith-community host sites; about 40 spaces with meals, showers, laundry and case management; intakes take place weekday mornings and Mesa's emergency-solutions funding supports this shelter.
resources.hours: I-HELP intakes: 8–10 a.m., Monday–Friday, at 2146 E. Apache Blvd.; call first to check availability.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Overnight emergency shelter for adults experiencing homelessness, operated by Tempe Community Action Agency (TCAA) through a rotating network of faith-community host sites in Tempe. Participants receive a safe sleeping space each night, evening meals, shower and laundry services, and intensive case management and resource navigation aimed at moving from the street to shelter to housing. Daytime resources at TCAA's services site include computers and phones, employment help through TCAA's Financial Success Center, emergency to-go food bags and a hydration station. The shelter serves up to about 40 adults at a time.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Adults who are experiencing homelessness, men and women. Intakes are completed in person Monday–Friday, 8–10 a.m., at 2146 E. Apache Blvd., Tempe. Call first to check availability and intake rules; a City of Mesa resource list notes that I-HELP does not accept individuals with sex-offender status. Whether the Mesa funding contract gives priority to particular households (for example seniors or couples) could not be confirmed — ask staff what is currently being accepted.

**Population Served**
Adults experiencing homelessness in Tempe and the East Valley, including men and women. Mesa's emergency-solutions grant funding supports this shelter for FY 2025/26, and City of Mesa and East Valley shelter lists include it among options for people in the area.

**How to Best Connect**
Call TCAA's I-HELP line at (480) 590-5514 to schedule an intake appointment, or come to the intake site at 2146 E. Apache Blvd., Tempe, between 8 and 10 a.m. Monday–Friday. Call before going — space is limited (about 40 adults) and a bed is not guaranteed. TCAA's services-site front desk is (480) 422-8922, ext. 5882.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no published fee to stay in I-HELP. Demand has historically been higher than capacity — program materials describe far more people seeking shelter than beds available — so call early and have a backup plan. TCAA's website lists separate I-HELP shelters in Mesa and Chandler run by other organizations, so if you are in Mesa, ask TCAA which program fits your situation. Host-site schedules, intake rules and bed availability can change; treat this listing as a lead to verify by phone, not a guaranteed place.

The 'Mesa seniors, adults and couples' descriptor was not confirmed and is flagged in the text; TCAA's own site shows Mesa I-HELP is run separately by another organization. The program itself remains a referable East Valley shelter option, so this is not needs-resolution.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Emergency financial assistance for people in crisis — including help with rent payments and utility/energy bills (Project SHARE assistance for SRP and APS customers) — plus emergency food boxes. The site also operates as a cooling center/heat-relief location (listed as Monday–Sunday, 11 a.m.–5 p.m.; hours can vary). This is stabilization help, not shelter: no shelter beds, housing units or motel-voucher program are listed for this location.

**Eligibility Requirements**
People in need who live in the Chandler, Gilbert or Sun Lakes area and who have not received funding from this Salvation Army location in the past 24 months. Funding is limited and not guaranteed even when you qualify, and an application/screening process applies. Mesa households are outside the documented help area — ask about eligibility before applying.

**Population Served**
Individuals and families in financial hardship in the Chandler, Gilbert and Sun Lakes communities. Services are available in English and Spanish.

**How to Best Connect**
Call 480-963-2041 and leave a message about your rent or utility need — this location handles assistance requests by phone message, and staff return calls. You can also visit 85 E. Saragosa St., Chandler, during general hours (Monday–Friday 8:30–11 a.m. and 1–4 p.m.; a separate listing shows service hours of 8:30–11:30 a.m. and 1–4:30 p.m., with food boxes Tuesday–Friday mornings). Call first to confirm you are in the service area and that funds are available.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no fee to apply. Do not promise a motel or shelter voucher through this location: current Salvation Army and 211 listings show rent/utility assistance, food boxes and heat relief, not shelter or motel vouchers — ask when you call in case programs have changed. Assistance is limited and allocated first-come; even eligible households may be turned away when funds run out. Hours and services can change seasonally — verify by phone before going.

resources.description: VA one-stop center in Phoenix for veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness: housing assessments and coordinated-entry referrals for transitional and permanent housing and eviction prevention, plus health care, employment help, benefits and community referrals; walk-in, no referral required, free of charge.
resources.hours: Mon–Fri 7:30 a.m.–4 p.m., excluding federal holidays; walk-in clinic — arrive early for same-day referrals.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
A VA one-stop center for veterans who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Staff complete housing assessments and refer veterans to transitional housing, permanent housing and eviction-prevention programs, and place eligible veterans on the community-wide housing priority list — this is the veterans' coordinated-entry site for the Phoenix area. The center also helps with immediate food and shelter needs, job training and employment referrals, justice-system navigation and community reentry from jail, financial support to prevent homelessness, addiction and depression treatment, and health and dental care. The National Call Center for Homeless Veterans, 877-424-3838 (877-4AID-VET), answers 24/7.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veterans who are homeless or at risk of becoming homeless — including veterans transitioning from jail. No referral is required, there is no cost, and you can walk in with or without an appointment. Bring identification and any military/VA paperwork you have; some on-site health services require VA eligibility or enrollment in a VA homeless program.

**Population Served**
Veterans and veteran families experiencing homelessness or housing instability in Maricopa County, including veterans leaving jail or prison.

**How to Best Connect**
Walk in or call: 1500 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 106, Phoenix, AZ 85014; phone 602-248-6040; email VHAPHOCRRCStaff@va.gov. Open Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4 p.m., closed federal holidays. It is a walk-in clinic, so arrive as early in the day as possible — same-day referrals, including to transitional housing, may not be possible if you arrive late in the afternoon; if that happens, staff can still provide community shelter referrals. After hours, call 877-424-3838.

**Important Information to Know**
The center is in central Phoenix — plan your transportation from Mesa. No referral is needed to walk in and ask for help, and services are free of charge. A housing assessment is not an immediate placement: referrals depend on program capacity and the community priority list, so timelines vary. Veterans who also need health, mental-health, benefits or employment help can often start those services during the same visit.

resources.description: HUD-VASH pairs a HUD Housing Choice Voucher (rental assistance for a private-market apartment or home) with VA case management and supportive services so veterans experiencing homelessness can move into and stay in permanent housing. Veterans connect through VA — the Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center (602-248-6040, walk-in) or the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans (877-424-3838, 24/7).
resources.hours: Walk-in access at the Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center: Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. (excluding federal holidays); arrive early for same-day referrals. The National Call Center for Homeless Veterans phone line is answered 24/7.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Permanent supportive housing for veterans: a HUD Housing Choice Voucher that pays part of the rent for a qualifying privately owned apartment or house, paired with ongoing VA case management and clinical support — including connection to primary care, mental health care and substance-use treatment, help with budgeting and leases, and long-term support to remain housed. Vouchers are administered locally by public housing authorities in partnership with VA, and the Phoenix VA homeless programs team handles referrals for Mesa and Maricopa County veterans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
For veterans who are experiencing homelessness and need ongoing, intensive case management (for example, due to chronic health conditions or other complex challenges). Veterans must be eligible for VA health care and meet HUD-VASH income limits — as of HUD's 2024 policy change, initial income eligibility is set at the Low level (80% of area median income) for all housing agencies, and service-connected disability benefits are not counted when determining income eligibility. A referral through VA is required; veterans cannot get a HUD-VASH voucher directly from a housing authority. Veterans who do not need intensive case management are usually served through other VA or community programs.

**Population Served**
Veterans — including veterans with families — who are experiencing homelessness in the Phoenix VA catchment area, which includes Mesa and Maricopa County.

**How to Best Connect**
Call or walk in to the Phoenix VA Community Resource and Referral Center (CRRC): 1500 E. Thomas Rd., Suite 106, Phoenix, AZ 85014; phone 602-248-6040; email VHAPHOCRRCStaff@va.gov. Hours are Monday–Friday 7:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m., excluding federal holidays. It is a walk-in clinic, so arrive as early as possible for a same-day referral (very late arrivals may instead receive a community shelter referral). Veterans can also call the National Call Center for Homeless Veterans at 877-424-3838 (free, confidential, 24/7) or ask their VA primary care team or social worker for a HUD-VASH referral.

**Important Information to Know**
Cost: the voucher pays the portion of rent above what the veteran contributes — generally about 30% of adjusted monthly income; utility allowances can adjust that amount. A referral does not guarantee a voucher, an available unit, or a timeline — voucher and case-manager capacity are limited, and the veteran must find a landlord who accepts the voucher; ask about current local availability when you call. HUD-VASH is separate from the regular Section 8 waiting list (Phoenix's regular Housing Choice Voucher list is currently closed); the City of Phoenix Housing Department administers HUD-VASH vouchers with the VA (about 903 vouchers awarded), and referrals still come through the VA, not the city.

resources.hours: Supportive Services for Veteran Families: Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–4 p.m. and by appointment; aftercare: 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; residential campus open 24/7; case management by appointment. Call before visiting — hours vary by program.
resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Transitional housing for veterans experiencing homelessness with wraparound support (case management, life skills, counseling, career training, VA benefits assistance); on-site permanent supportive housing where veterans can take over the lease; SSVF (Supportive Services for Veteran Families) rapid re-housing and homelessness-prevention help, including rent payments, security deposits, moving costs and transportation; free mental health and substance-use counseling; employment and career services; aftercare case management after a veteran moves into permanent housing. Housing campuses include the M.D. Hawkins Veterans Center (opened 2026, with a dedicated wing for women veterans) and Ashley's Place, a transitional housing program for women veterans.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Veteran who served in the active military, naval service or Coast Guard with a discharge other than dishonorable; must be homeless or at imminent risk of losing housing; very low income for most services. Permanent housing programming is aimed at veterans who can live independently and are economically self-sufficient. Ashley's Place serves women veterans who experienced military sexual trauma, intimate partner violence or domestic violence during or after service and who can live independently in a shared housing environment; eligibility screening applies. Typical documents: photo ID, DD Form 214 (or letter of service) showing discharge status, recent proof of household income, proof of homelessness (or current lease and eviction notice if housed), and Social Security cards for household members.

**Population Served**
Veterans in Maricopa County, including women veterans and veteran families. U.S.VETS Phoenix reports it supports more than 300 veterans experiencing homelessness every day and has served more than 10,000 veterans since opening in 2001.

**How to Best Connect**
For transitional housing, call the outreach team at 602-757-9723 or 602-859-7329. For SSVF and family housing help, call 602-441-0612. Main line: 602-717-6682. Offices: 3507 N. Central Ave., Suite 200, Phoenix, AZ 85012; residential campus: M.D. Hawkins Veterans Center, 12027 N. 28th Dr., Phoenix, AZ 85029. Calling, emailing or visiting the office starts the process; veterans working with VA can ask their VA case manager to refer them. Hours: SSVF Monday–Friday 7 a.m.–4 p.m. and by appointment; aftercare 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; residential site open 24/7; case management by appointment.

**Important Information to Know**
Most services are free; transitional housing fees vary. Program openings, beds and screening outcomes are limited — call ahead to confirm current availability, and do not count on immediate placement. Some programs serve specific groups (Ashley's Place: women veterans; SSVF: very low-income veteran households). Hours and program details differ by service and can change; confirm by phone before traveling.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Coordinated entry and assessment for families with children under 18 who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness in Maricopa County: connection to family emergency shelter (including placement on the family shelter waiting list), diversion help that can resolve a housing crisis without entering shelter when possible, a short- and long-term housing plan, and referrals to rapid re-housing, transitional housing and permanent supportive housing programs. The Hub also connects families to other community resources (food, benefits, employment, health care) and serves families that include a military veteran.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families with children under 18 who are homeless or at risk of homelessness. Families should call (602) 595-8700 before going in person, and all adults 18+ in the household are required to take part in the call or visit. An assessment does not guarantee shelter or a housing voucher — referrals depend on eligibility and limited availability.

**Population Served**
Families with dependent children under 18 in Maricopa County, including Mesa. Help is available in English and Spanish.

**How to Best Connect**
Call (602) 595-8700, or dial 2-1-1 (877-211-8661). UMOM recommends calling 2-1-1 or checking 211arizona.org before visiting to get matched with the best resources for your family, including options that may prevent homelessness. Location: 3307 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85008 (near the UMOM campus); program website: fhhub.org. Families already on the list use the Hub's check-in number for weekly check-ins. Confirm hours by phone before traveling — published hours differ between sources.

**Important Information to Know**
There is no fee. Wait times are the main challenge: in September 2026, more than 200 families were on the family shelter waitlist with waits described as about three months (Mesa has cited 2–4 month coordinated-entry waits); ask about diversion, rapid re-housing referrals and 2-1-1 options while you wait. Earlier community guides listed Mesa-area entry points (Mesa CAN at 635 E. Broadway and Save the Family at 125 E. University Dr.) on certain weekdays, but later notices said the East Valley and West Valley sites were closed and families should call the main line — confirm current options by phone. If the fhhub.org website does not load, call (602) 595-8700 directly.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**
Heat-relief respite for families with minor children experiencing homelessness: a 24/7 space with daytime and overnight shelter (including cots in indoor tents when the site is full), meals and staff support, operated on UMOM's Phoenix campus during the extreme-heat season. UMOM also assesses each family for diversion and shelters those who cannot be diverted, and provides hotel stays as overflow when respite capacity is full. The program served more than 700 people (more than 440 children) by mid-September 2026, and the city reported more than twice as many families served as in summer 2025.

**Eligibility Requirements**
Families with minor children who are experiencing homelessness. Access is by referral — the City of Phoenix contract specifies referrals from other heat relief sites and City of Phoenix outreach workers; there is no public application or walk-up intake for the hotel stays. Families should be assessed through the family homeless-services system (call 2-1-1 or the Family Housing Hub).

**Population Served**
Families with minor children experiencing homelessness in Phoenix and the surrounding Maricopa County area. UMOM is the region's family coordinated entry provider and the state's largest family shelter provider.

**How to Best Connect**
There is no direct intake line for this program — referrals come through heat relief sites and City of Phoenix outreach teams, and UMOM's own guidance for families in a housing crisis is to call 2-1-1. Families with children can also call the Family Housing Hub at 602-595-8700 for assessment and shelter referral. UMOM main line: 602-275-7852; campus: 3333 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85008. Ask specifically about summer heat relief and family shelter availability when you call.

**Important Information to Know**
This is a seasonal program tied to the heat season, and 2026 availability is time-limited — the City of Phoenix contract runs through October 31, 2026, and UMOM reported extending heat relief through the end of October 2026. Capacity has been under heavy strain: in September 2026, some families with hotel stays were reportedly told to check out earlier than planned while UMOM looked into the cause, so treat hotel availability as limited and confirm at the time of need. The service is city-funded; no family fees are described in the contract. Outside the heat season, use 2-1-1 and the Family Housing Hub for year-round family shelter and housing help.

**Services Offered**

Emergency shelter on the UMOM New Day Center campus for households with children. Families receive private rooms; fresh meals served 7 days a week; one-on-one case management; employment services and job training (including UMOM's Homegrown culinary and warehouse/logistics tracks); help connecting to benefits such as WIC and unemployment; advocacy with property managers, landlords and courts; connections to community resources; help finding permanent housing, including housing vouchers when available; rapid rehousing and permanent affordable/supportive housing pathways after shelter; on-site children's services, including an on-site Boys & Girls Club and a children's health clinic run by Phoenix Children's Hospital; adult health care through partners (Health Care for the Homeless and Circle the City); and daily school bus service that keeps children in their home school.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Families with dependent children (children under 18) who are experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County. Families are screened, prioritized and placed on the shelter waitlist through the Family Housing Hub, the single countywide coordinated entry point for families, rather than applying directly at the shelter. Families that include a veteran can also access support through the Family Housing Hub on the UMOM campus.

**Population Served**

Families with children experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including larger families (a 2022-2024 county-funded expansion targeted families averaging six members) and families with non-traditional heads of household. UMOM reports serving about 75% of families in Maricopa County shelters and sheltering roughly 155 families (about 800 people) on campus each night.

**How to Best Connect**

Start with the Family Housing Hub: call or text 2-1-1, or call 602-595-8700 (also 877-211-8661); online at fhhub.org. UMOM asks families to call 2-1-1 or visit 211arizona.org before going in person so they are matched with the best options, which may include help to avoid shelter. The Family Housing Hub is at 3307 E. Van Buren St. #108, Phoenix, AZ 85008, next to the UMOM campus at 3333 E. Van Buren St.; intake is handled by phone and English/Spanish are available there. UMOM's main line is 602-275-7852. Confirm current hours and any in-person arrangements before sending a family.

**Important Information to Know**

No fees are charged (211 lists no fees for the shelter or the Hub). Placement is not immediate: UMOM manages the single countywide family shelter waitlist and reported in mid-2026 that more than 200 families were experiencing homelessness and in need of shelter; capacity and waitlist status change daily. Length of stay varies - recent UMOM participant materials describe a short-term emergency shelter stay (30 days) focused on diversion and housing search, while older materials cite stays of up to 120 days - so confirm current terms at intake. Shelter is a step toward permanent housing; a 2024 county case study reported 802 individuals moved into permanent housing from the program that year.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Emergency shelter specifically for single women, with rooms shared by two or three women and private bathrooms. Residents receive fresh meals served daily; one-on-one case management; employment services to help secure and keep a job; advocacy with property managers, landlords, courts and partner agencies; connections to community resources; and help with the search for permanent housing. The center serves up to about 130 women each night and is designed for single women without children.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Single women age 18 and older who are experiencing homelessness; no children in their care for this program (women with children go through the Family Housing Hub instead). Victims of domestic violence are explicitly included, but the shelter is not limited to domestic-violence survivors. There is always a waiting list for shelter.

**Population Served**

Single adult women experiencing homelessness in Maricopa County, including survivors of domestic violence. UMOM describes Halle as the first shelter in Arizona designed specifically for single women.

**How to Best Connect**

Call the Halle Women's Center intake line at 602-362-5833 to get onto the waiting list for shelter. Reported intake hours are 6 a.m.-2:30 p.m.; administration is Mon-Fri 8 a.m.-5 p.m.; the shelter operates 24/7. Location: 3424 E. Van Buren St., Phoenix, AZ 85008, across the street from the UMOM main campus (3333 E. Van Buren St.). UMOM's main line is 602-275-7852; program information is at umom.org/find-help.

**Important Information to Know**

No fees are charged (211 lists none). A bed is not guaranteed: there is always a waiting list and availability changes daily. A 211 listing marks the exact shelter location as confidential even though UMOM publishes the street address - call before going. Women with children, or women who need a confidential domestic-violence placement, can also call the 24-hour SAFEDVS line at 480-890-3039 (toll free 844-SAFE-DVS), which UMOM lists as the domestic-violence shelter route for Maricopa County.

resources.informationText:
**Services Offered**

Historically, this included a youth crisis shelter in Maricopa County for unaccompanied minors ages 12-17 (known as Open Hands under UMOM/Tumbleweed), providing shelter, food, counseling, education support and family reunification, with longer stays and life/workforce skills for youth who could not return home; and independent living programs for youth ages 16-21 (including young parents with minor children) providing housing, case management, counseling, life skills and transportation help. It is not confirmed that UMOM still operates these programs; Child Crisis Arizona is the documented current operator of the county's Safe Place youth crisis response and of the former UMOM Independent Living Program.

**Eligibility Requirements**

As historically described: unaccompanied minor youth ages 12-17 for the crisis shelter (a legal guardian must be located within 24 hours of entering shelter), and youth ages 16-21, including those with minor children, for independent living/transitional programs. Current eligibility must be confirmed with the operating agency before any referral.

**Population Served**

Youth experiencing homelessness, runaways and youth in family conflict or unsafe situations (ages 12-17), and transition-age youth preparing for independence, including youth aging out of foster care (ages 16-21) - based on the historical program descriptions for these services.

**How to Best Connect**

For immediate safety and shelter for a youth 12-17 anywhere in Maricopa County, call or text Safe Place: 602-841-5799, or text 'SAFE' plus the youth's location to 4HELP (44357). Safe Place sites include all QuikTrip and Valley Metro locations. To ask whether UMOM still operates any youth crisis shelter or independent living services, call UMOM's main line at 602-275-7852. Do not send a youth to the former UMOM/Open Hands youth shelter address without confirming who currently operates it.

**Important Information to Know**

Operator unresolved: UMOM's current website and referral pages describe shelter for families and single women only; in 2021 UMOM announced that Child Crisis Arizona took over its Youth Independent Living Program, and Child Crisis Arizona announced it became the home of Safe Place in Maricopa County (the 12-17 crisis line above). Some older profiles and directories still attribute a 12-17 youth crisis shelter and the 16-21 independent living program to UMOM, and reported bed counts differ (6 vs. 10). Because a misdirected referral could put a minor at risk, treat this as a lead to verify, not a confirmed placement route; the Safe Place line is the supported current entry point for youth 12-17.
